coimge): co tardad nech urcomded de, .i. co tarta cach
in comdethbhirus dlegar de lit. equal (full ?) justification, i
236.15. gen comdethbhirius turbaidh air, 286.w. fiadhain
. . . ria cach comdethbirius, 300.30. coimdedh .i. coim-
dethberus, ut est fo coimdedh .i. fo coimdethberus, O'C.
1423 (H. 3.18, 638a). coimdi .i. comdedberus, O'Dav. 580.

n, [f.] (déitiu) act of acknowledging (fully ?), acknow-
ledgement: dég dligid comditen (-in, MSS) dána, Críth Gabl.
320 `on account of right and acknowledgement and (or `of')
office', n. senchomditiu tuaithe, 322 `longstanding sub-
mission', Gloss. chis comdidean fria triar `rent acknowledged',
Laws v 450.3. ? ingraide tire comdidan `jointly fenced
land', iv 48.13, cf. a comaititin, 18 Comm. In passage
on `rudrad': deit[i]u didiu saegal comarba, aititiu saegal a
dó, comdetiu saeghul tri fir. Is ann as rudrad o rosaigh
co coiciur
three generations amount to c. (
full acknowledg-
ment?), ZCP xii 363.19. na rudredui becci . . . déitiu ina
cedbliadan, aittitiu ine tánaisiu, c. in tress, 23. dicoimnigh
comdeitin tir comarbe cen taiselba, O'C. 2459 (Eg. 88, 37a).
Follg. etymol. glosses may have second element -dítiu:
fri fortacht noibre in coimded .i. fri foirithin na hopri dliges
a comditin a tigerna de, Laws iii 22.21 Comm. mad inol
beas la coimdid .i. conid comditin é, v 80.19, 21 Comm.
Note also: fáise . . . in sciath o chomdhiden do chuirp `from
before your body', Ériu viii 22.21. See comdeddaid.

(delb) equal (similar) shape, form; (equal) manner:
hicomdeilb randatad gl. in eandem notitionem, Sg. 188a9.
dom' chomdeilbsi, doAdam (words of God), SR 1824.
doch., 1828. fo chomdeilb `in like fashion', Met. Dinds. iii
368.22. fon coimdeilbh cetarobia
in the same form in which
she was first, Anecd. i 79.3. cruth ┐ c. . . . cach ríg, LL 31096
(TTr.). láich do samla ┐ do chomdelba, TTr.² 765. teora
ocmnai . . . comaesa(ib) comdelbæ, IT ii 179.151. comor
comdelba re athair, TTebe 2689. ? hicondeilb frisin brethir
`in conformity with the verb', Sg. 52b1 (scribal error for com- ?).

o, ā (comdelb): a Michol merda . . . / . . . com-
delbach of symmetrical shape, SR 5990.

(comdelb, cf. con-delba): curub é in spirut is
prem coimdelbtha don craidhi `the root which forms the
heart', Rosa Ang. 128.7.

i, m. (comdelb) one of the same shape; likeness,
image: do Adom dom' ch. (words of God)
my image, SR
838. 2173. tabair oirmitiu . . . dom choimdelbaidsea, LB
109b53 (MacCarthy 44.19) = choimdelbaigi, YBL 157a5.

(deimin) very certain, etc.: C. c., LL 30484 = corr
deibig, Met. Dinds. iv 8.12.

form.p:
gl. dominari, Ml. 17b1. Cf. coimdemnacht
(see Ped. ii 62).

egForm.p:
(com + dénam, cf. con-déni): hi comdenum
pectha friu `in doing sin equally with them', Ml. 34a23.
In follg. = dénam: dam orda . . . do crutacad ┐ do comdenum,
BB 241a28. aní bhíos arna choimhdhéanaimh do cháilibh
contrárdha, TSh. 3156.

eg.p:
Lib. Hymn. 12 gl. 84. Leg. -demnach
(demon) ?

form.p: gl. comdetae, LU 7379 (BDD 100).

egForm.p:
[f.] (deóin) mutual agreement, consent: is comhdheoin
do niatt eturru(dh), Laws ii 270.21 Comm. coirpdire . . . do
reth riss a comdheoin, 144.21 Comm. cach uair is comdeoin
leo araen `whenever they are both mutually satisfied', iii 442.18
Comm.

(derb): co mba c. isín mbit[h] nach sgēl `equally
known', Death-tales 12.7.

(derg) very red: ba c. . . . a eich `all red', TTebe
2913. cor-ba c. do chru, 3285.

(dérgud): for comdergud fri ríg sharing
a bed with,
LL 24444. See comdéirgide.

(dess). Of persons ambidextrous; expert (somet.
in vague laudatory sense): in chland chomdess, Met. Dinds.
iv 68.146. mulier ambidextra non fit .i. ni fhédann bean a
bheith coimhdheas, 23 K 42, 112.19. an cruitire coir coimh-
dheas, Leb. Gab. 284.12. a Shaoir choimdheis cháich (of
God), Measgra D. 61.64. ni bi . . . ceard ar nar choimdheas
an D. sin expert, Ériu iv 51 § 8. ba coimdes ar gach trea-
lamh troda, FM vi 2234.17. sai coimdes coitchenn in cech
cerd archena, Ann. Conn. 1309.2. ba c. isna primbelraib
well versed, LB 150b42. As sobriquet: Corcan coimdes `the
handsome', Gorm. Jan. 7. C. c., `the Comely', MR 206.4.

eg.p:
Other applications: ic dáil chomdeis Ch., Met. Dinds. iii
224.4. crathad cruaid, comhdhes, MR 256.7. gersat . . .
comdesa . . . cimsa . . .catha, 254.4. iarsin charddine chóir
ch., LL 16100.

Of equal alternatives in various constructions: is cuma
lium .i. is cóimdess lium cipé dib, Thr. Ir. Gl. 9.29. is
coimdes doibh muir ┐ tír `they are equally at home on . . .',
Maund. 267. air is coimdes di-sside tairissium o ḟotaib ┐
cuimrib (of metre)
can consist either of . . . , IT iii 101 § 180.
conidh coimdeas a cumasc fri ceachtar na da rannaidecht,
BB 289a25. coimdes a airlegind sis ┐ suas `indifferent',
Auraic. 5827. comdheas re da chlaidemh, L.Chl. Suibhne
10. ní la nech . . . dinn ná caislén . . . acht coimdhes da
gach aen iatsom `each has an equal right thereto', Marco P.
139. gus in inad ar chomdeis do chach a chomfhégad
`where all might conveniently view him', MR 180.20. ba
comdeis imbualta da deis ┐ da cli, Cog. 186.6. Superl.
duine is comdeisi . . . i cantairecht, ALC i 270.2. Adv.
ar cách co comdess `in order due', Met. Dinds. iv 222.22.
hit chomfocus co comdess, Fing. R. 720. Cf. comdas s.v.
comadas ?

egForm.p:
= dess (a) (see D 46.61 ff.): cruisecha catha a com-
desaib curad, Ériu viii 30.28.

(déicsiu): hi comdēscin na flesc `looking at',
Otia iii 48 § 7.

(dían) (very) vigorous: na slúag saindían / cuman
comdīan `with like vigour', Arch. Hib. ii 61 § 43 (LL 23660).
Adv. co coimdian comluthmar, BB 244b11.

(do-bádi): ro comdibdaid `were quelled', CCath.
6030 v.l. (-digbait, text).

eg.p:
robad fherr lim c. duib, Aen. 2698 `I would rather
ye strove along with us(?)', Gloss.
see comdiubr-.

egForm.p:
(díchra) equally (very) eager, zealous: comdicra
bar curaid, MR 126.10. da chert-bheim . . . comdichra,
298.20. na catha . . . coimdhícra, CF² 1042. Adv. co
coimdichra `with equal fervour', CCath. 5538. 5849. Hugh
Roe² 262.19.

(comdíchra): ar comdichracht a comraic
`keenness', TTebe 3124.

[i, m.] (comdídnad) comforter: a comdidantaid
na toirsech (of Holy Spirit), Hib. Min. 43.18.

u, m. vn. of comdídnaid. Also -íthnad (see Thurn.
Gramm. 81) act of comforting, comfort: act of helping, rescuing:
dessimrecht comdíthnatha gl. consolari eos, Wb. 14b11.
dilgud et c., d1. ní bíth chomdidnad damsa indib, Ml. 62b6.
87d1. 4. ishe se incomdíthnad, Sg. 90a7. c. (comdignaibh,
MS.) (.i. comsasad) iarsna saethraib, Trip.² 219. no bidh
angel Dé ica comdídhnadh, RC xxvii 302 § 76. dolluid int
angel . . . do chomdiugnad P., Anecd. iii 37.16. comdīdnad
(comdignad MS.) torsi `a comfort of grief', BColm. 96.9. in
spirut otá cech cómdignad ┐ cech comairli don eclais,
IT i 169.14 (FA Eg.). tuc cobair, tuc comdidnad, CF 89.11. ac
comdingnad a cheli, TTebe 1848. ro guidhset . . . ima coim-
dingnad o nert in diabail, Grail 4204. a c. ┐ a fortacht, PH
4286.

(dídnaid, see do-dona) comforts, consoles: ro
choimdidnasstair indi naem Muiri ind fhis, YBL 156b21.
roscoimdidnus, 155b17. nos-comdhidnand A., Aen. 1216.
comdídantar he i n-a mogadu
he is comforted in his servants,
PH 6576. Vn. comdídnad.

(dígaind): craebchaill comdigainn very dense,
CCath. 4109.

vn. of comdíglaid: ic comdigail a chnead ar chach
`revenging
his wounds', MR 248.25. a tigerna . . . gan coimh-
digailt, Caithr. CC 75.

(díglaid): do chomdiglais do chneadh `thou hast
sufficiently avenged thy wounds', MR 170.20. Part. com-
dígalta, 244.6.

(diglaim): lá garma i gceann coimhdhioghluma,
DDána 89.19 `choice gathering', Ir. Monthly 1920, 317.

(com + dil): da comalta comdili do rig alaind E.
equally dear to, BB 237b53. As subst.: a comdili his friends,
ZCP xxx 138.28. Cf. cunnail.

(díl): siad ar-aon ag coimhdhiol cliar rewarding to-
gether, Magauran 2026. C. da ccoimhdhíol, BNnÉ 287 §
275.

(dile): nis fuar caem a chomdile
I never found a
friend so dear, LL 5146 (Bruchst. 70 § 163, Auraic. 5339).

(díles) (equally) forfeit, alienated, irrecoverable,
belonging, etc.: comdiles cach smacht fri colainn a feich,
O'C. 60 (H. 3. 18, 21b). coimdhiles dire, Ériu xiii 16.19.
comdiles do cach dib cia tarta dia raile (of spouses), Laws
ii 350.20. cis lir . . . ada comdilsi do cach recht?
which are
common property? v 482.23 .i. . . . is comdiles doib he ┐
do cach richt duine, 484.7 Comm. is comdilius don fir nod
cendaig . . . ┐ don fir o ngatar
equally the property of, O'C.
661 (H. 3. 18, 323). do-fhacaib Dia cech maithius cómdíles do
chách `a common possession', PH 7553. a bheith coimdīless
[do] nāsion sa chrīstaighecht toigecht gusin aonach sin
`that any nation . . . had the right of coming', Fl. Earls
150.13.

(dílmaine) complete freedom (from liability),
liberty: tres-na pecthaib do lecud i c. do cách `in full liberty to
all', PH 4164. fo chomus ┐ fa chomdilmaine a chuirp
force
and capacity, MR 270.15.

eg.p:
(dílse): foracba a cuit tire la fine a comdilse dara
eise
what land remains to him must revert to the fine
in joint
ownership, Laws iii 52.10. ? ni roich colann coimhdilsi
n-einech, Ériu xiii 13.22. Of adversaries: comdílsi etruib
fair play between you, PH 741. doleig coimdisli iter na
curadaib `fair field', TTebe 4474. coimdhilsi do lécen etorra
┐ M.S.
to leave the issue between him and M.S. (?), Acall.
1977. rainic coimdilsi ann etir longaib bronn na sochaide
┐ claidhme muintire C. (of slaughter in battle), CCath. 5745.
releíc comdílsi etarru ┐ in snechta
left him at the mercy of the
snow (of infant being abandoned), RC xxvii 264.4.

egForm.p:
(comdílse): ro coimdilsighset na dromanna (leg.
a nd.?) do muintir Cesair turned
their backs on (i.e. in flight),
CCath. 5751.

(dín) act of (mutually) protecting: C. diar coimdhíon,
Gorm. July 25. dlighidh rí cách do choimhdhíon, DDána
80.1. ilceda a[c ?] comhdin aroile `for mutual protection(?)',
St. Ercuil 1256.

na c. cin fri faiche `the debt is not to be equalized
to the distress in the green', Laws ii 124.2.

(2 dindba ?): ma comuaisle no ma comdinnba
equally wealthy(?). O'D. 540 (H. 3. 17, 443).

(díne) contemporary generation; coeval(s), associate(s):
dom aes chomtha ┐ dom chomdínib, ┐ dom chomdínib,
Táin 1861. dichairdib dichomdíneib, SR 5916. ra chind
ar a chomdinib, TFerbe 641. rogrād fir alathīre / romsīacht
sech a comdīne `beyond all his mates', Ériu ii 15.x. doghēn-su
. . . / comrádh ar mo choimdíne, Anecd. i 28 § 25. beag nar
bháidh clú a choimhdhíne, Magauran 3805. Of a tree: ni
crand acht taidbsiu ṡídi / ní marat a chomdíni `its kind',
Ériu xiv 160 § 32. gs. as adj.: trícha bó . . . / do búaib
caéma comdine
of the same age, LL 37881 (SG 363.21).
lucht c., Acall. 2450. In phr. is c. do x
is a contemporary,
associate, of x: is iat is c. dam, Acall. 4442. ba comdine do
Ch., LL 2693.

(díre), equal `díre' fine, equal honour-price: .u. seotu
comdire cac cnis `equal mulct', Bretha 27. c. do rig ┐ epscop,
ZCP xvi 175.y ( Laws i 40.15). a comdirib, a comriaraib,
O'C. 1907 (23 P 3, 23(21)d). is aire conaimes na comdire
seo i cuic setaib, Laws v 476.27. ro suidiged i coimdiriu
for .vi. setaib (of bishop or `saí'), 390.8. dlighid comdiri
cuma fri a righ, Anecd. ii 75.9. As adj. of equal `dire'
fine, entitled to equal `díre' fine: comdire la feine . . . ge,
corr, caitine, O'C. 2478 (Eg. 88, 38 (39)d). comdire diguin
┐ bas, 2627 (Eg. 88, 53 (54)c). deich cerda comdire (of types
of verse), IT iii 59.12.

With FRI: c. a ben fri cach recht hi mesaib croligi `his
wife has equal dīre
with each class', BCrólige 3. hi comdire
fri a huasal neimthiu cethra, Laws iv 198.z. comdire ollum
fri rig naen tuaithe .i. comeneclann, O'C. 1950 (H 4.22, 5).

(dírech) (equally) straight, upright; just: enadharc
ḟada choimhdhirech, Ériu v 190.466. co ceimeannaibh . . .
comdirgae, St. Ercuil 234. na colamain coimhdirigh `up-
right', CCath. 4201. is comiuir .i. is comdíriuch hic hícc
namaithe, Fél.² xxv gl. 229 = O'Dav. 1100.

(comdírech): treb Z. i cómdírgi trebe N.
in the same
direction as, LB 126a2.

(dírgud) act of directing, guiding: d'ár cobhair,
d'ár comdírgiud, MR 306.26. do chomdirgiud Clann C.
ar forbaisib foréicni `to protect . . . against violent assaults',
144.13.

(díth): for commarbad ┐ comdith destruction, BB
432c31.

eg.p: see comd(e)itiu.

egForm.p:
(do-bidci) hurls; pelts: rochomdibraicid . . .
bera aithgera iarnaidi, TTebe 3086. Vn. coimhdiubhrag-
[adh], RC xi 320.2 (TBC). na clocha cruindi comdibh-
raicthi `easily hurled', TTebe 1984. lasna coimdiubraicthibh
`by the shots', Hugh Roe² 180.28. a[c] comhdiurucudh
E., St. Ercuil 469.

(díumuss) (excessive) arrogance: im chomdimmus
in trír curad sin, LU 8560 (FB 42). ro ferad cath . . . fo
comth(t)uilg ┐ comdimus o curadaib, BB 432b29.

(díupart): innrecht .i. comdiubairt, no nemrecht
(joint) fraud, O'C. 108 (H. 3. 18, 70).

eg.p: see cuindliged.

egForm.p:
o, ā (dligthech) Legal equally legitimate, adjusted:
fiach comdligthach `lawful', Laws v 178.18 Comm. masi
comdlighthi[g] iat, 482.7 Comm. sena in ḟir don mnai masa
comdlighthech iat `equally admissable to give evidence', ii
350.15 Comm.

(dlúith) compact; (equally) dense: catha comdluthi
ceṅgalta, LL 32462 (TTr. 1657). na neoill coilli comdluithi,
TTebe 4842. clardroichet . . . comdluith, CCath. 5825.
comhdhlúith a gcath, DDána 111.19.

(dlúm): cuic cumala ina chomdluim chorpdha
compact mass, O'C. 1041 (H. 3. 18, 435b).

(dlús): ar a cc. `so compact
were they' (troops), Cog.
173 n.5.

vn. of comdlútha(ig)id. act of compressing,
consolidating: tre chomdlúthad gl. per sineresin (gramm.),
Sg. 117b1. 118b3. a clarad ┐ a comdlutad (of the Temple),
BB 241b28. teaghdhaisi treabar-dhaingne do c[h]omd-
lūthugadh, ML² 82. a comdhluthadh `it's binding together'
(of alphabet), Auraic. 1021. do chomhdhluthugadh a
g-cairdeasa re reimheas na rignaide rempa
to unite, MR
86.10. Cf. nacomdluta gl. compaginum, Lor. Gild. 233.
roscailset a comdluta `they sprang leaks' (of ships), Aen. 258.

(comdlúith) condenses, combines, makes com-
pact: rochomdluthadh in múr, Rawl. 74b2 (BB 7a1). ros
comdlúthaig i ndíb cossaib `held it close between his two legs',
Táin 772. comfuaiges ┐ comhdluthas (of successive biblical
texts), Fen. 4.1. Intrans.: gur comdluthaigseat na catha re
cheli, Marco P. 61. Vn. comdlúthad, -ugad. Part. comdlúta.

part. of comdlúthaid. compressed, condensed:
.vii. cneslénti (sic leg.) . . . clártha comdlúta, LU 6413 (TBC).
cathair caem comhdlutha, KMMisc. 316.2. imdha comdluthta
`an enclosed bed', Ériu viii 121.18. In military contexts: at-
cumsctha comdluti na catha, Cog. 196.29. ina cipe comdluta
cobsaid, Ann. Conn. 1256.6. Of wooden artifacts: soidhech
do claraib comdluthta `closely-joined', Marco P. 65. clárdh-
roichet comhdhluta, FM vi 1896.7.

eg.p: c. gort icthair aichthe, IT iii 99.4.

egForm.p:
(dochar) equal hardship: dorinne a ccomhdhochar,
BNnÉ 219.z, v.l. an comhdhochar coitcheann, TSh. 7717.

(dóig, see doich): mad comdoigh a fhaghbail do
neoch aile ┐ d'a tigherna féin `equally likely', Laws v 326.22
Comm.

eg.p:
(dolud): a gcongnamh na gcomhdholadh `their main-
taining of simultaneous obligations(?)', Aithd. D. 76.2.

(domain): condoman .i. com-doman, Corm. Y
258. go ndernai classaigh comdomhain `deep entrenchment',
CCath. 2477. gusan cclasaigh ccomhdhomain, Hugh Roe²
18.26.

egForm.p:
(comdomain): condoman .i. com-doman .i.
c. deepened, Corm. Y 258.

(donn): im tríchait Corpre comdond very brown,
TFerbe 900. co C. na clad comdond, Met. Dinds. iii 358.42.

vn. formation from comdonn: gan bhrat cclúimh
do chomhdhonnadh to dye dun, brown, IGT Decl. ex. 1270.

(dorchae) very dark; obscure: intan bis dlighthe na
rann comdorca gl. cum sunt partium jura obscura, O'D. 848
(H. 3. 17, 603). dona haichthib c. cumascda, TTebe 2337.
tar chisealaibh c. . . . na calad, ML² 690. a n-étaigib
comhdhorcha, Fl. Earls 254.11. a gcomdhorcha na hoidhque,
14.25.

(dorchugad): an tegh aga comdorc[h]vgudh
getting dark, Aisl. Tund. 113.9.

(dord): comdhord ciúil `un chant de basse', RC xxiv
380.3.

vn. of comdortaid: in c. daronsat a namait con-
certed attack, CCath. 2675. ar c. na cath-laem, MR 226.4.
comdortadh i ccenn shocraitiu Ui D., Hugh Roe² 334.12.

(cf. do-fortai, doirtigid) pours out (trans. and in- trans.), flows copiously: ro comdoirtset tri ruadbuinne . . .
fon domun, CCath. 4327. le ccomhdhortar a charthannacht
a gcroidheadhuibh a chlaine
is lavished upon, Luc. Fid.
3410.

form.p: Vn. comdortad.

egForm.p:
(1 dos): Bili Tortan Eó Rosa / at comáille comdosa
`as . . . bushy', Ériu iv 150.24.

eg.p: see drantaigid.
.i. malum .i. comolc, Corm. Y 345. See 1 droch.

egForm.p:
(drut): a[c] comdrud a edaig `pressing together',
TTebe 3739. ag a comdrud i gcenn a chéile, MR 256.22.

(dúal): dias dan[a] comhdhual cáisi belongs equally,
Met. Gl. Ff. 75.

eg.p: see condúala(ch).

egForm.p:
(dúalas, see dúalgas): cona chairdib ┐ cona ch.
for in tṡlúagud `his friends and his kin', Táin 355.

(dúan): ar chrithribh caola comhdhuan measured
poems, Hackett² vi z.

(doilig): i nAird Chaindlech c. (:tuirim) `forlorn',
Met. Dinds. iv 238.44.

(duine): uachdarán nó íochdarán, no cómhdhuine
equal, De Imit. 190.14.

(dul): ceithre cnairre na cc. `going with them', Leb.
Gab. 96.7.

vn. of comdúnaid: ier gcomhdhūnadh uile dhorass
na heguilsi `had been closed', Fl. Earls 52.1. an chloch . . .
ag comdūnadh a bruit, 172.29.

part. of comdúnaid: isin carcair comdhúnta `close
prison', Hugh Roe² 12.3.

(dúnaid): da comdunta cro cadhat na cath-
latraig . . . air
if . . . encircled him, MR 262.10. cómh-
dhúnamois leis na briathraibh so conclude, De Imit. 132.w.

form.p: Vn. comdúnad. Part. comdúnta.

eg.p: c. duras rig, Ériu xvi 65.37 (rhet.).

egForm.p:
(dúthaig) belonging equally by hereditary right;
natural: c. dóib . . . / . . . in ríge `a like inheritance', BR² 780.
Cog. 212.20. 130.8. ní comhdhúthaigh dá gach cléir / an
sduagh . . . bhoinnréidh `not of the same family', Magauran
4051. ní fhuil peacadh mór ná mion / nach comh-dhuthaigh
dá ciniodh
but is natural to, Dán Dé xxi 16.

(dúthchas) equal right of heredity; inherited
instinct: co comdūchus in cuirp, Anecd. v 23 n.26. coibin-
tius no comducus don [ḟ]ine `inherent right', Laws iv 208.1
Comm. comduchus ceirt C., Cog. 54.11. leth Midhe . . . a
ccomdúthchas dóibh `their own inheritance', 130 n.3. Predic.
gs.: uair ba comduthchusa comcheneoil . . . cuingeda `of
equally noble descent', MR 246.2. Concr.: a lámhaibh . . .
ar g-cómhdhúthchasa `co-relatives', ML 102.10. do chada-
duibh na ccomhdhúthchus (of related letters d, t etc.),
IGT Introd. § 103.

(dúthrachtach) equally, very zealous: na
catha . . . comdhúthrachtacha, CF² 1042. Adv. co comsann-
tach comduthractach, CCath. 2762. 5538.

(ecor) array, ornament, proper arrangement; as vn.
act of arranging, adorning: in comlinad ┐ in comegur `the
number and array', CCath. 3122. for comecur a cath, LL
31965 (TTr.). co rathairrngid urrsanda na cathrach as a
coimegur `proper position', TTebe 4421. do coimeagar
cloidem ┐ craisech ar a cheile `mutual hacking', MR 266.26.
coill . . . ar na comhecar do challaib crimhann `adorned
with', Ériu iii 156.13. lec logmar lasamuin . . . i comecur
in tigi `adorning', TTebe 318. .l. gem . . . ina chomecor (of
goblet), Acall. 2194.

Attrib. gs.: cathbairr coemegair `ornamented', TTebe 1529.
cona cobradaib coimeccuir `adorned bosses', CCath. 4727.
d'ór is d'aircet coimecair, Acall. 808. Predic. ba comecair
aireacht
it was an orderly assembly, ZCP xi 62.3.

Legal `putting an equal stock on the land', Laws iv 92 n.l.
i tir dibadh ata ín comecur sin, l Comm. coimheccur in
fearaind athar ┐ seanathar, O'D. 2409 (Rawl. B 506, 52b) =
1189 (H 2.15, 69b) = 1562 (H 5.15, 3a).

(ecartha): cathbarr . . . clárach c. well-arranged,
LL 24889.

(ecla) (great) fear: re crith na comeagla, MR 232.4
(coimegla, LL 409a30). TTebe 2736. crith comeclai, LB
118b3. gnē imfhaitchis ┐ choimhegla orra, Fl. Earls 54.w.

(eclach): do guth ard, comeglach, crithanach
terrified, ZCP vi 41.30.

(écmais): a gcoimbfhēgmhuiss a n-atharrdha
`far removed from', Fl. Earls 242.9.

(ecraid): rocomecrad leosum comrair don mac
`was arranged', TTebe 2209. rocomecrad . . . teni, 2221.

eg.p:
míle comged (leg. c., Corrig.) a ḟoscad, Met. Dinds. iii
146.6 `its shadow stretched a thousand cubits', Corrig. where
c. taken as com + 2 ed.

egForm.p:
(ad-opair): hi[s] sruith in fer c.
to whom thou makest
sacrifice (?), Arch. iii 316 § 40 = comoipre, LB 261a58.

(éicen) constraint, oppression: cnead osnadach
comeigin (leg. -gne) C., MR 260.9. gan chánaigh gan choimh-
éigean, DDána 82.8. Attrib. gs.: cach cathchoma chomégni
chuingeas, MR 122.7.

eg.p: see con-éicnigedar.

egForm.p:
vn. of con-éicnigedar. coimheignedh, Smaointe
B. Chr. 2511. act of compelling, constraining; compulsion:
turtad .i. coimēgniugud, O'Mulc. 866. cen comeicniugud
o nach aile, Ériu vii 148.25. tre chomeicniugad peindi
`by restricting(?) [the period of] penance', xix 58 § 6. comeic-
niugud broit na bidh `compulsion of raiment or food', ii 144 §
161. iarna coimeicnigud ona treablaitibh. Lism.L. 689.
gan coimhéigniughadh (of breath), Reg. San. 20.11. naire . . .
ima coimeicniugad, Grail 3059. L., ag coimhécniughadh
na manach docum oibre `driving on', BCC 294.10. ní
féadtar a choimhéigniughadh, TSh. 5168 `he cannot be com-
pelled', Gloss. arna choimhégniughadh . . . do thrégen an
tṡáoghail =
constrayned . . . to abandon the world, RSClára
34b.

(éicse): isin topur the / dianid cocur ceól-éicse
(comeicse, v.l.), Met. Dinds. iii 288.40.

(éigid) shouts aloud, shout together: ro-chomegetar
na hIúdaide, PH 2617. 2835. ro-chomégitar ┐ atrubratar,
2606. 2743. do coimheighidur . . . ag iarraidh Isa do
chrochadh, Smaointe B. Chr. 3886.

etc. (see in-loing): [mad] i cunn comlann c.
.i. o comeillgis iad a comlaintis a ceille codhnaigh is joined(?),
bound(?), O'C. 2405 (Eg. 88, 31 (32)d) = 1081 (H. 3.18, 443a).
See also s. 3 coblach.

(as-lena): iars a ni comeillnither corp ┐ ainim ac
denam cinad `are defiled', Laws iii 96.8 Comm.

(éirge). Vn. of con-érig. coimérghi, f., IGT Decl.
§ 3 (44.31). Verbs § 83. act of rising up (together). Freq.
of warriors setting out, mustering for battle; attacking, assault-
ing: in comerge dorigni in pheist, LU 9101 (FB 85). lasa
comérge conérracht (in figura etymologica), 4880 (TBC).
fir Hérend . . . ac c., Táin 4666. barbardacht na comérgi
assault, MU² 116. a laithi an c[h]oimēirgi / bid caomha a
cuirp, ZCP viii 215.35. rapa phrapp in choméirgi, Ériu xiv
157 § 9. comerge co foltaib, ZCP xiv 382 § 47 (see 383).
otchondairc P. . . . na genti do choméirghi fris
rising against
him, Trip.² 490. ní . . . soairle coimērgi frit mac `to rise up
against thy son', Ériu i 118 § 8. ba coímeirghi im choraidh
comeirghi imbe, LL 406b20. comerge trom na namat forro
assault, Anecd. iii 67.23.

eg.p:
With follg. gen.: co folmaiset ind fir comergi debtha dorísi,
LU 8419 (FB 29). i comérghi in catha sin `to begin that war',
CCath. 232. atraachtatar U. . . . ra frithálim coméirgi
bréithri L. `to answer the summons of L.', Táin 4640. ma's
do comeirge in comraig atracht `if they mutually arose to battle',
Laws v 256.24 Comm. tri c. curad 'na coimeirgi
accom-
panying him, Caithr. CC 16.

Of rising to the feet as sign of homage: fíadh .i. airmitiu
do cach fo gradh, dar liumsa issí in comeirge hí `rising up
(
to salute)', O'Dav. 875. gan chis, na gan chomergi `nor
tribute nor obeisance', MR 186.14. comeirghe do denumh
ime cein beit a suidiu `to do homage', Laws ii 194.12 Comm.
diabludh comerghe, 14 Comm. ní fuair coimhéirge remhe,
RC xxvii 296 § 59. ag so a Chríost do choimeirghe (`this
is what we pray of Thee'), Content. xvi 200 (see n.).

(éiric): comeric ┐ comdire doib
equal `éiric', O'C. 221
H 3.18, 117). ní imgaib comeric, ZCP xii 262.30.

egForm.p:
(éirim). Attrib. gs.: 'na charput chobsaid chomerma
`firm, rushing', RC xiv 400 § 5. dom fhior choimhéirme ┐
chaomhrúin
of like interest(?), DDána 104.4.

eg.p:
artificial compd. arising from perfective forms of
as-ren. Only in Laws Comm.: is é cin . . . i nuasal comer-
nither feich gl. asrenar, Laws iii 156.16. cidhbe uasal comeirnes
a n-ic gl. as-da-comra, v 182.18. 346.33. 348.18. comméd
. . . na cotach . . . ro uasal comeirneastar dar a ceann gl.
is comren, O'C. 392 (H. 3.18, 219b). Note also: innsaighim
co ro comerne ria fine in gl. on críth, O'Dav. 425. connacht
.i. comerne ut est ni condacht in cin . . . o apad in bi[d]badh,
O'C. 576 (H. 3.18, 286) = comeirnedh, 1475 (H. 3.18, 653).
see coibéis.

egForm.p:
(eiséirge): amal rongab comadnacul duún, atá
comeisseírge gl. consurrexistis, `co-resurrection', Wb. 27a15.

(éitsecht) act of hearing, listening (to): cid senchas
túachail re techt / don Chrúachain ria cométsecht, Met.
Dinds. iii 354.84. ag coimhéisteacht fris an tír `watching',
FM vi 1936.22.

ni bid coblach nad bi comglinne .i. noch coir c. itir
manab comdaingen é, O'D. 555 (H. 3.17, 438) `to compose',
O'Don. Suppl.

eg.p: see aindísc.

egForm.p:
(eneclann) equal eneclann, honour-price: im
comeneclainn doib `equal honor-price', Laws i 42.26 Comm.
c. fri rig T. do, Anecd. ii 76.5 v.l. comdire .i. c., BCrólige
4 n.l. a c. gl. indogbāil doeir, Anecd. v 26 n. 8. As adj.
coimeneclann gach da gradh dib so, Ériu xiii 33.1. duine
as coimheneclann ris, 50.10. comheneclann cach dibh
fri ceile `equal honour-price for each with another', BCrólige
5 gl. l. i comdam ┐ comeniclann é ┐ in rig buden,
Laws v 74.19 Comm.

eg.p:
diam aon cuid comennaig ailius, O'C. 2482 (Eg.
88, 39 (40)a). See ennac.

egForm.p:
(éolach) equally wise, skilled: in tan robitis coimeo-
laigh, Aen. 1067. da feithemain . . . comeolach, O'C. 1193
(H. 3.18, 475a). is cóimheólach sinn uile uirre `equally
acquainted', Atlantis iv 132.17.

io, iā part. of con-erchloí: ind andaig comer-
chloithi gl. coactae malitiae, Ml. 80b4. gl. acti, 54b16.

as. (airmitiu): dober c. feid fris fessin . . . do
doinacht maic gl. aequalitatem honoris, Ml. 127d10.

(airsclaige): oc cathugud ┐ oc comérge ┐ oc
comersclaig[i] `arising and fending', TTr.² 1071.

(esorcon) collision, coincidence: c. do dib ordaib
etarbuas, Laws iii 188.15 Comm. masa comesorgain a da
coman eturra fein, O'C. 2376 (Eg. 88, 29 (30)b). massa c.
doidbi (leg. do díb) naeraib i nenḟecht, O'D. 2391 (Rawl.
B 506, 48c).

brufidhi a catracha, c. a mna, ZCP xxx 113.5
(BB 490b5). Cf. con-nesa(?), commus(?), 186 n.

(see next): ind árd (=i n-árd-) ch. `Chief Com-
missioner', FM v 1816.2.

dp. (based on Engl.): le commessieoraibh
Luimnigh `Commissioners', FM v 1802.5.

(étgud). Attrib. gs. cona hoctur inghin . . . comēt-
gudha
having the same clothing, ZCP xiii 175.26.

(étiud): conad ceó comlethan . . . in c. sain, LL
32205 `that clothing' (warriors' breath), TTr. 1394.

(fadód, see atúd): comf[h]adōd fīc[h]a strong
incitement, ML² 1125.

(fáes(s)am): coibsena .i. confessiones .i. com-
fæsaime, Corm. 11. i comḟaesam . . . ris budein `to equal
protection', Laws v 12.24 Comm. in tollam brethemun . . .
comfaesam . . . e. ┐ in rig
has equal right to grant safe keeping,
O'C. 276 (H. 3.18, 151 half-leaf 13).

(fáilte) joint welcome, joy: cennsu ┐ comhfail[te] ┐
trōcaire, Otia ii 96 § 27. do fheratar na cléirigh comh-
fáilte fris, Misc. Hag. Hib. 102.19.

eg.p: see comphairce.

(cf. forcsi): rosc corr-glas . . . lais is e claen
comfaircsech (of Hector)
viewing on all sides(?), BB 427a37.

egForm.p:
(faire): i comfod ┐ i comfhaire watching together,
MU² 220 v.l.

(fairsing) very extensive, expansive: in ceathar
duil comairsiṅg, TTebe 3080. tar crislagib comf[h]airsinga
na cisel, ML² 672. prīmh-chathoir chomhfhairsing, Fl.
Earls 36.21. Of person: bheith cómfhairsing fial, Oss. iii
232.18. Adv.: go comhfhairsing sa ffairrgi, Fl. Earls 8.13;
19. As subst.: ar comarsing in láir ┐ in tigi
whole expanse,
LL 31776 (TTr.).

(fáiscid): comh-fháisgthear gach neach lé téadaibh
= constringitur, TSh. 7483.

eg.p:
(faísitiu): cobais .i. comais .i. comḟaisitiu, Corm.
11 = ón chomfaoisitin, Corm. Y 292.

egForm.p:
(faitches): ní cabhoir in comhfaitcheas `equal
anxiety(?)', Duan. Finn ii 164 § 36.

eg.p: see cobfán.

(fann): comfand gl. comlabur, Laws v 470.16
Comm. (466. 21).

egForm.p:
(2 fás): ar bhfearg ó do-chí ar ccomhḟás
on the increase,
IGT Decl. ex. 941. Cf. cobás.

eg.p:
do neoch is conntabairt do torrachtain do denam
na gaide ris nar labuirsit na c. lan fir no lan arra, O'C. 2428
(Eg. 88, 33(34)d). See ad-suidi, comastai.
see comḟot(a).

egForm.p:
(feb): Cathaīr cōem Conn comfebaib (comfedmaib,
v.l. / fallnathar flaithemdai, Corp. Gen. 70.9 = `mit gleichen
Tugenden', Ält. Ir. Dicht. ii 14.y.

(febsa): fo chomdáil, fo ch. `with likeexcellence',
Met. Dinds. iii 288.36.

eg.p: see con-féga.

nó fíoradharc gl. comchissi, Triads, p. 39 § 119.
See féchsain.

form.p: (fégad)

egForm.p:
(a) act of viewing, watching: imram cach
coblaig. ri c., LL 31972 (TTr.). do chomfhegad a cusaile,
MR 114.23. i comfhegad in catha `looking on at the battle',
234.13. Note also: dol do coimhfhéghain Chláir Néill `to
inspect', TD 9.54 (O'Gr. Cat. 408.21).

eg.p:
(b) esteem, consideration: C. cana choimégad `that C.
should not be held in high regard', BR² 2011 = comḟeghadh,
BB 281a25. gan chomfhégadh comaltais `without regard to',
MR 298.21. gan chaigill, gan ch. `without consideration',
160.13. 200.20. 226.2.

egForm.p:
(feidm) joint (equal) effort, exertion: C. . . . / com-
febaib (comfedmaib, v.l.) fellsatar, Ält. Ir. Dicht. ii 14.y.
cach . . . fo coimfeidm isin cat[h], CCath. 5849. comfheidm
catha `joint effort of battle', TTebe 2814. Attrib. gs.: ar
cuibhdhi coimhfedhma, Anecd. ii 37 § 6. fo mbiat catha
comlebra (is chomḟed[ma], v.l.), Ériu iv 106 § 55. fochacht
comḟedma, SR 3454. coimfhedma Treóil is Cú Chulaind
`are equivalent', Stud. Hib. iv 61 § 4. ar toirnem chuingida
choimfedma `well-matched', TTebe 1098. Note also: bith i
fothrib co ferda / dognítis co comḟedma `sharing hardships',
Met. Dinds. iv 326.26.

(feithem) act of watching: ráith choimhfheithmhe,
DDána 117.29.

(cf. feódaigid): bacan . . . do maid(h)e cruaidh
coimhfeodhaig[th]e (very) withered, BNnÉ 191.5. coimh-
féoidhe, 26.

(fer) partner, companion: comfer tíre tuinid, O'D.
1607 (H. 5. 15, 12a) `occupier(?)', Plummer MS. notes. com
fer tire tuinide, O'C. 337 (H. 3.18, 185b). mo choimhfhior
coguid, Phil. ii 25.

(feraid): crú an chridhe do choimhfhearais shed
copiously, Aithd. D. 603.4.

(ferda): sa cath cródha choimhfhearrdha `manly',
Duan. Finn ii 48.6.

(ferg) (mutual, fierce) fury, anger: fō chomḟeirg, Otia
ii 88. balotar ass tria comḟeirg `equally angry', Táin 1462.
ar cruadbach ar c. `fury', CRR 5. chum cennairrce no
coimhfeirge, BNnÉ 237 § 161. le cóimhfheirg a cheile
with anger toward each other, ML 140.21. coimsig cruth a
coimferge, SG 251.28. c. curad, LL 31461 (TTr.). Attrib.
gs. ar chongalaib chomfherge C.
fierce attacks, MR 224.15.
With FRI: um coimhfheirg frisna cléirchib, SG 70.7. a ch.
catha fri Crūachain
battle-fury against C., Bruchst. 16 § 29
(IT iii 88 § 103).
(fergach): co comfergach `angrily', ZCP vi 282.21.

form.p:
(fergaigid): rocomfergaid he became angry,
TTebe 2517.

egForm.p:
(fert, see fiurt): ní fhuil náemh . . . / . . . / rosoisedh
coimhfherta fri B. equal miracles, BNnÉ 35 § 57.

eg.p:
sibill an(?) comhfhetta, BLism. 109vb1. Cf.
coimét?

cā[i]d cach rēt co canōine comūaim (c., v.l.), Corm. Y
1224.

egForm.p:
(fíach, cf. cobach) equal debt, liability: is comfiach
in raith ┐ marbadh, O'C. 484 (H. 3.18, 251). cíos ┐ coimh-
fíacha mora, BNnÉ 232 n. Predic. gs. it coimfeich la Feine,
Laws v 458.5.

(fíachach) equally liable: it cobfīachaigh . . . fir
┐ mnā, Cáin Ad. 45. As subst. cetheora comfiachaigh
four
parties equally liable, Laws iii 264.16 Comm. cethrur
comfiachach, O'D. 1572 (H. 5. 15, 5b).

(fíadnaise): in tan dosnegmaic im comḟiadh-
nuise joint witness, BCrólige 46 n.3. i c. fri ríg, Críth Gabl.
497. comrath ┐ coimfiadnuisi `equal testimony', Laws ii
282.2 Comm. ar mbeith do Dhía ag déunamh coimhfiádh-
nuise ríu, Heb. ii 4.

(fíal): C. coimḟial, Acall. 97 `generous', Duan. Finn ii
86.z. a Ch. chruthglain comfeil, RC xx 142.19.

(fíalchaire) joint friendship: no co ro scuirea a
eochu i tir fine ar coibfialchaire, Laws iii 382.8 Comm. =
ar comfialchaire, O'D. 1982 (Eg. 90, 11 (12)b) = ar
coibhdilichus .i. ar comfialcaire, O'C. 2541 (Eg. 88,
45 (46)b).

form.p: (fíalus)

eg.p:
(a) kinship, relationship: ier ffios a ccairdesa
┐ a ccoimfhialusa, Leb. Gab. 224.20. gs. as adj. muna
rabhadar coimḟialusa no combraithri cheana, BB 301a16.
cen cunn coibialussa `without a chief of the same tribe', Laws
iv 24.15 Comm. cen cunn comfialusa ris, 26.18 Comm.
fine comsloinnte .i. comfialusa, O'D. 549 (H. 3.17, 437).
Gramm.: ata ind aipgitir ina . . . comcengal litrioch cona
comfielus archena, Auraic. 2721. 4937.

(b) kin, relative(s): fri a choimfhialus ┐ chomhfhuilidhe,
Leb. Gab. 222.15. roadnaic cach . . . a chomfialusa ┐ a
chomuilidhe, Ériu viii 56.6. ar ceann a ngaoil ┐ a gcoimh-
fhialasa, Keat. iii 5168.

egForm.p:
= comḟíalus (b): a comialusta kinsmen, BB
237b46. caim na carat . . . na commuilidi na comfialasta,
241a45.

(fían): do chluiche fri comḟíannaib `fellow-warriors',
Met. Dinds. iii 40.24.

(fid) in etymol. glosses on cubaid (metr.) corresponding
letter; having corresponding letters(?): coibhḟíodh . . . ar an
ní as ionann fiodh airegdha, Ériu xiii 43.33. cach da cobfid
i cubaid `every two corresponding letters', Auraic. 957. is ed
a chubhaidh intan is cobfhidh, ┐ is cobfhid in focul ind
imfrecra `the same in vowel', 1513. cétchuibdius i coim-
fedaib, Eg. 1782, 54b1 cited Meyer Contribb. (`musical
instrument made of wood').

(fíchda): an dís crodha coimfhíochdha `fierce',
Duan. Finn ii 48 § 60.

(fillte): ara ngluinib . . . comfillti `bended knees',
TTebe 2534.

(filltiugud): comfhilltigh[th]e ┐ comshuidhigthe
`derivatives and compounds', Auraic. 1900.

(Engl. (re)fined): d'airgeatt ghlan choronta na
Sagsan comhghlan, comhfhinailte, RIA Trans. xv 89.4 of
text.

madi comind fia fiadna .i. ma dia comfindaig,
O'C. 525 (H. 3.18, 263a) = comhfinnaigh, O'D. 703 (H. 3.17,
514) (see Laws v 420 n. ).

form.p: (fis)

eg.p:
(a) act of visiting, inquiring for: dotaet . . . F.
. . . do comfis a athar `to learn about', Dinds. 118. do-thāet
. . . do ch. a meic, Corp. Gen. 87.17.

(b) (joint) knowledge: cen ḟis (ch., v.l.) do neoch aile, ZCP
iii 3 § 3. masa da c. `if of their joint knowledge', Laws iii 134
n. 2. See cubus.

egForm.p:
(flaith) joint rule: M.N. . . . i comlaith ┐ C.C.,
LL 319b37. Corp. Gen. 190.8. ré .u. ṁbliadna i c., LL
14968 ( MacCarthy 176.8). dīblīnaib i comflaith, ZCP iii
464.32. arra cuir cuirmthighe comhḟlaith, Ériu xiii 34.18.
Attrib. gs. an dís curadh comhfhlatha `equally princely',
Duan. Finn ii 48 § 59.

eg.p:
Note also: E. ┐ C. comflaithi joint rulers, Corp. Gen.
117.45.

egForm.p:
(flaithemnas): da mac A.S. i comflaitheamnas
joint sovereignty, Anecd. i 2.24 (SCano 39).

(flaithius) joint, equal sovereignty: trí ríg bátar
for hErind i comḟlathius, LL 2515 (Dinds. 161). com-
flathus do ┐ do N., MacCarthy 298.16. a comflathus fri
hIuil, 302.26. 306.27. co mbemis a comflaithius, Aen.
2683. i comhflaithes gan cinned (of the saints in heaven),
BNnÉ 274 § 249. cómhḟlathus do bheith eadtortha, Ériu
i 82 n. comḟlathius for Herind, LL 3154. C. ┐ E. i com-
flaithis fo[r] Erind, Dinds. 132. ro gabh Ereamhon ┐ Emhear
comhflaithius os Erind, FM i 26.7. comlaithius gach
mathiusa eter nem ┐ talam `lordship', Celtica iv 10.48.

eg.p: see 1 coibled.

egForm.p:
(fliuch): neoill comh[fh]liucha `misty', TTebe 1963.
na clár cóimhfhliuch (of the sea), Atlantis iv 144.13.

(fliuchaid): mōr ndear do chomhḟliuch da cíur
.i. mōr mban do līon dá grádh, ZCP v 489 § 11 (B. na f.).
Vn. frais . . . / . . . do choimhfhliochadh cháigh to drench,
Ir. Syll. Poetry 52 § 6.

(cf. fo-botha): fer comtren . . . comfobthaith,
IT ii2 246.64 Eg. `equally terrible', Meyer Contribb.

(foccul): na ceithre comhfhocail cuibhdhi `maxims',
MR 90.3. as comhfhocail an Eaglas Chatolic ┐ an Eaglus
Rōmhánach synonyms, Mac Aingil 6027. Gramm. nida[t]
. . . comfocail `full sounds' (of semi-vowels), Auraic. 462.
comfhocul = prepositio, 321. = conjunctio, 301. comḟocul
gl. hec coniunctio, Ir. Gl. 873. In IGT compound: do chomh-
fhocal no d'ainm úathaidh, Introd. 1.22. na gnéithe don
Ghaoidhilg nach cóir a ttús chomhfhocal, 2.18. don fhocal
déigheanach don chomhfhocal téid a cheannus ┐ a cheart
[┐] a innsgne, § 136. c. canamhna `a compound whose first
part has elided vowel', Bard. Synt. Tr. p. 140. .l. . . . greim
comhfhocail, nó comhfocal canamhna a ttús comhfhocuil
cheirt, 17.2. IGT Introd. §§ 97. 100. comfocul lochtach,
Metr. Faults §§ 1, 28, 129. 'na shamhail do chomhfhocal
(of `Scitia'), Keat. i 234.9.

eg.p:
(fochain, see fochonn): is fích co mbúaine
mothair / crích Gúaire don ch. `for that cause', Met. Dinds. iv
16.z.

form.p: (fochraíb. See O'Rahilly, Celtica i 341-3).

eg.p:
(a) in phr. i c. near. With gen. hi comfocraíb imdai ind ríg,
LU 7648 (BDD). i comḟochraib ┐ i comḟacus in dorais, LL
31094 (TTr.). a comhfocraibh in tsleibhe sin, CCath.
1221. a comfocraib na cairrcci, Grail 2149. ar a chom-
fochraip
near it, Fl. Earls 122.30. With DO: i comḟocus ┐ i
comḟochraib dóib, Táin 2125. rancatar i comaichraib do B.,
RC xiii 72.9. Absol.: in slog i comfocra, Laws v 192.23 Comm.

(b) With copula and DO: combu comochraib báss dí,
near her, Trip.² 2345. 2712. gorbo comfochraibh . . . doib,
CCath. 3881. ba comhfoc[h]raibh don caiscc, ZCP x 411.10.
Note also: mad comacraib iat ┐ madh comaith a torodh
`equally near' (of bees), Laws iv 172.25 Comm. Attrib.:
isna ferannaibh comacraibhibh
in the neighbouring districts,
Anecd. iii 64.5. oc milled . . . na crīch ┐ na cennadach
comfochræib, Arch. iii 224.16. morcaisléin in leit[h]e com-
focraib don G. `of the side near to G.', CCath. 3432. na
feranna comfochruibhe, TFrag. 196.19. is na tírib com-
fochraibe, TTr.² 624. na da chiniud chomfochraibe, Laud
610, 90a, cited Meyer Contribb. s. comḟochraibe. Adv. co
comfochraib i [co]mfocus
very near, CCath. 2417.

egForm.p:
Subst. neighbour(s); neighbouring territory: nach déni olc
fri-a chomfhochraib, PH 8090. comfocraib a[c] cainedh a
chele `neighbours', Aen. 2720. Iotar na comfochraibhe día
nagallaimh, Leb. Gab. 242.30. na comhfochraibh battar
comhfoiccsi dóibh
his nearest neighbours, FM v 1786.6. an
bá forrél do na comfocraibhe do'n domhan `neighbouring
parts of the world', iii 10.3. isna comhfhochraibhe `in the
neighbourhood', Hugh Roe² 42.22.

(comḟocal): crist comfoclach `of like name', Fél.²
clxxii 36. gasra chearrbhach chomhfhoclach `talkative',
E. O'Rahilly 130.169.

(fócra): ar gcíos [cáir dá] chomhfhógra `being for-
bidden', Magauran 3721.

form.p: (1 ocus). Also -(ḟ)acus. comgus, Keat.

egForm.p:
I o, ā near, proximate; neighbouring; equidistant. Predic.:
as comacus du bas, Ml. 40b9. as comacus a mbás, 64a2.
comocus afogur díblínaib (of u and digamma), Sg. 6a3.
rondgab coimdiu comacus les `that he has a Lord near'.
Ml. 30b11. atcumacsi ┐ atcumsctha . . . na catha, Cog.
196.29. Attrib.: hicómdail nalenab comocus `neighbouring
children', Fél.² xcix 30. comaicsi gl. uicinaeque (nationes),
Ml. 26b11. a foithrib na crich comfhogus, TTebe 4537.
na cenela comḟaigsi
related, BB 416b12. do bochtaib na
cell comḟocus bai doib `the neighbouring churches', RC xxiv
64 § 26. na gcinedhach gcomhfocus gusin teagh sin, Fl.
Earls 114.26. cidh nesa don indlighthech í ná don dligh-
thech, no cidh comfocus dóibh
equidistant from them, O'D.
509 (H. 3.17, 413). Compar. as chomaicsiu gl. uiciniore,
Ml. 145b2. combad chomaicsiu side dodia gl. in vicinia
Dei, 21d1. comfhocsi . . . do thalmain indas do esca, PH
6988. Superl. don chin dian ar comacsi in dibad, Laws iv
286.15 Comm. Adv. inchomocus gl. iuxta, Sg. 197a7. `near
by', 188a19. gluaisid airdrinnaidh na speiri . . . co comfada
┐ go comhfogus da ceili
equidistantly, Ir. Astr. Tr. 132.7.

form.p: II As subst.

egForm.p:
(a) proximity; relationship: ba crombaing caem
a comḟagus `relationship', BB 50a38. rannait iar comocus
in proportion to their nearness of relationship, O'D. 548
(H. 3.17, 436). iar comfogais colla
nearness of blood-relation-
ship, O'C. 2234 (Eg. 88, 17(18)a). fine teachta iar comfocus
coibfine, ZCP xiv 372.13 ( Laws ii 282.z). im comfogus Crist
gossipred, Laws v 364.11 Comm. Attrib. gs. fo lin cenn
comocuis `according to the number of kindred heads', Laws
iv 284.4. dibad cach cind comacuis, 284.2. do cert com-
focais `by right of relationship', 44.8. coibhdelach comfocais
don cintach
near of kin to the debtor, O'D. 584 (H. 3.17, 446).
a fine comogais `next of kin', Laws iv 128.5. dá cháirdibh
comhguis, Keat. Poems 133.

eg.p:
(b) In concrete sense relative(s), stock; neighbour(s):
im-fuich cach curu(d) a comfocuis
contracts entered into
by kinsmen, ZCP xiv 371.1 Hūi M. cona comḟocoss, Corp.
Gen. 58.15. bar mbrāithri ┐ bhar comhḟoiccsi `neighbours',
RC xxv 392.17. nocharad in comhfhocus amail hé féin,
Lism. L. 4876. is ionann comhgas nó comhfhogus ┐ gaol,
Keat. i 68.45.

In phr. i c. (do) near (to): diar tigh fil i comoccus dun,
Vita Br. 37. i comfocus dona apstalaib, LU 1991 (FA 6).
i comḟocus ┐ i comḟocraib dóib, TBC 2434. With gen.: i
comfhacus a chesta, PH 1676. a comhfhogus C[h]., ML² 356.
see cobodail.

egForm.p:
(cf. con-fodlai): traigid comamserda comfodlaide
equally divided, Lib. Hymn. 64.13.

eg.p:
(fogal): iar gcách do chomhfhoghail
having attacked
all and sundry, DDána 109.6. maoin iar mionoghadh 'ga
chrobh fa chomhfhoghal (of generous patron), Hackett²
xlvi 4.
See cobodail (supra).
see comfoigelt.

egForm.p:
(foglaimm): a cheile comhghaisgidh ┐ comḟogh-
lama
his companion . . . in learning, ZCP x 276.10 (RC xi
330.8).

eg.p:
(fognam): ag comhfhognom do Dhia serving
God, Fl. Earls 140.32.
see con-fograigedar.

egForm.p:
io, iā part. of con-fograigedar: isin litir com-
ḟograigthi `consonantal letter', Sg. 15a4. As subst.: donaib
comḟogrichthib archuit tuisil gl. partibus incipientibus a
consonantibus, Sg. 221a1.

eg.p:
(comḟograigthe) consonantal: comh-fhog-
raightheacha .i. fograigit malle fri guthacha, Auraic. 368.
consoin onni is `consanantes' (sic) comfograightech, 2749 =
Lec. Gl. 214. consain comfograigtech, Auraic. 2760.

egForm.p:
= comḟograigthech: consain comfograigh-
thid, Auraic. 375. Adv. in chomfograigthid gl. concinnenter,
Ml. 42d12.

eg.p:
(fogur) = Lat. consonans: ní fail dechor comḟogair
indib gl. consonantis differentiam (of c and q), Sg. 6b2. Cf.
ónd nephchomḟogur gl. inconsonantia, 152b3.

egForm.p:
(oicse). Also -aicse. proximity, nearness: arar-
comoicsi dobás gl. responsum mortis habuimus, Wb. 14b25.
huan chomaicsi gl. a uicinia mortis, Ml. 82b1. incomaicsi
gl. viciniam, 78c7. gl. regionem, 121b10. amail mbis comaicsi
caich dia laile, O'C. 857 (H. 3. 18, 388a). ? ar comaicsi in
diba[i]d, Laws iv 286.15 Comm. o tainic dano comaicsi
laithe eistechta G.
approached, RC xlvi 233. 'na chomh-
fhoigse `near him', TSh. 3909. a comfoicsi do Ch. na M.,
Grail 1100.

(com(ḟ)ocus) approaches, comes near to;
brings near (trans.): comaicsigedar gl. adpropriare, Ml.
107b9. comaicsigfid Dia dún gl. contingetur
will draw near
to us, 53b17. continuans .i. a comoicsider `when it is made
contiguous (consecutive)', Sg. 59a2. ro chomḟoicsechastar
laithi éitsechta P. = adpropinquante die mortis eius, Trip.²
2965. rofitirsium coro chomacsig amser a chesta, LU 2313.
cōmocsigī gl. continuo, ZCP xxi 281.20 leg. comocsigim,
283 § 19. comaiscsit . . . a n-ænmaigin, TTebe 4724.
ro-t-comaicsigis o-t míadamla ar cumachta-ne `thou hast
approached our power with thy majesty', PH 3907.

eg.p:
Intrans. with DO: o ró chomaicsig dond ídul, Trip.²
1008. nocon ... o imluad cuirp chomḟocsiges nech do Dia,
Thr. Hom. 94.21. ra chomḟaicsigestar cách díb d'araile,
Táin 3294 = comfoicsigetar, St.

In Laws Comm. in etymol. glosses: dibadh cach cind
dar coimfoicsi[gh]ed in ferann (gl. comḟocais), Laws iv 40.19. gu
nícand cínta ín ti ra comhaigsigedh do (comoccuis), 288.7.
in ti ro comfoigsidegh (leg. -iged) do da caim fine gl. iar
comfocus coibfine, ii 284.16.

form.p: Vn. com(ḟ)oicsiugud.

egForm.p:
vn. of com(ḟ)oics(ig)id(ir). act of approaching,
coming near to (DO): comfaicsiugud don talam, CCath.
3943. di chomacsigud dina cathaib da céile, LL 32506
(TTr.). ro-b ail dó comfhoicsiugud do'n chathraig, PH
4422. In etymol. gloss: nis tic do cert comfocais .i. ní
tic do comocsigud de do reir chirt, Laws iv 46.18 Comm.

(fogelt) in etymol. glosses: congelt fri flaith .i.
in flaith do beith aca comfoigeilt, etc., Laws v 366.29-31
Comm. congellait. .i. cia lin da ta comfogelladh no com-
fogeilt, .i. co comtoirgit, i 230.9 Comm. Similarly (without
lemmata): [co]mhfoighelt risin Righ don cethrar, Ériu xiii
52.13. an Righ ar comhfoighelt riú, 16.

(see imchomairb) grumbling, complaint(?): cengat
cen chomfoirbb don chathrōi, Ériu vi 122 § 12. ? cen comoirb,
cen īr, Arch. iii 320 § 90. ? comarb do manchaib `rivalry(?)',
Celtica viii 62 § 10 (comorb, -oirb, -airb, commarbai, v.ll.),
cf. comairb.

(comḟoirb): nir bo comḟoirbech tra docos annsin
complaining(?), BB 436b4 = imchomairgech, LL 38875
`with much safeguard', TTr. 2092.

form.p:
gl. comparandam, Ml. 64c4 leg. comfoiridi, Edd.
(vbl. of necess. of con-foíra).

egForm.p:
(fóirithin) help, assistance. In etymol. gl.:
comfórithin, Laws i 300.9 Comm. gl. comruith, 268.2.
comḟoirithin gl. cobair, O'C. 421 (H. 3. 18, 230b).

eg.p:
da c. na naoi nae, Celtica ii 71.45 `perhaps a
back formation from comhfhurtach', note p. 87.

(folach): la hiliomat a n-arm . . . dia ccomfholach
`concealing them', Hugh Roe² 174.30.

egForm.p:
in phr. comṡuthain ┐ c. dond (frisin)
athair (of Christ, of the Holy Spirit), LU 2308, PH 6187
(-mḟ-); 1087, 3952 (-mm-); `equally to be praised' (see molb-
thaige), Stokes, RC iv 247; `con-substantial', Atkinson (as
if from folud). For the consonantal group cf. comḟuilid.
See comsolbthi.

eg.p: see foraithmiti.
see comorba.

lam ceill comforbaidh co tinard diairimter co
n-ethomair arathair (rhet.), LL 393a2. Cf. forbbaid(?).

egForm.p:
(for-beir): nagega chomforbrit gl. ramos con-
crescentes, Lor. Gild. 194.

eg.p:
(forcomét): robai i[c] comforchoimed gnima
caich `keeping equal watch', Aen. 734.

egForm.p:
(forlethan): is comforlethan a fuirmed ┐ a inde
(of the word
bonus) equally broad, Auraic. 3400. in teitged
is comairleathan i cintaige ┐ i slaintige
embraces both a bad
and a good sense, O'C. 1388 (H. 3. 18, 630ab) = 900 (400).

(fortacht). Also -ḟurtacht. act of helping,
comforting; help; comfort, relief: do comfurtacht an craidhi,
Rosa Ang. 140.8. aon-chomhfhurtacht = consolatio, TSh.
6569. dia chobair ┐ dia chomfhurtachtt, Hugh Roe² 162.4.
Día . . . na cumhḟurtachda = Deus . . . solatii, Rom. xv 5.
comhfhortacht bethadh `supplies', Fl. Earls 88.20. na
Gregaigh do comhfhurtacht d'E., St. Ercuil 2111. do
bhéaradh comhfhurtacht dó = qui consoletur eum, TSh.
4740. dorinne caomhna ┐ comhfurtacht dom' chill, BNnÉ
266 § 234. See comḟurtachtaigid.

(fortail): in cethrur crúaid c. `equal-strong', Met.
Dinds. iii 6.54.

(forusta). As subst. co tucatar a troighthi . . .
ar an comfarusda, Caithr. Thoirdh. 67.13 `the tableland'.

-ṡosad, -osad (fossad II, sosad, os(s)ad): is and
ro bói hi comḟosaud, i nDind rig
in residence, ZCP iii 7 § 22
v.l. dorónsat comhluighe ┐ comhosadh rest, FM ii 1064.3.
go com[s]osad Cind Slebe, Ériu viii 50.30. Us. meaning
truce: bud cotach bud comḟossad, LL 6906 (SG 373.3). do
denam chóra ┐ chomossaid fri Grecu, 31822 (TTr. 1010).
sith ┐ comsosud `peace and truce', Cog. 58.25. comsossod,
64.33. comosad dam sa . . . co ndechos . . . `give me time',
Ériu viii 34.13.

As vn. ag a chomhfhosadh for an crann `fastening
it',
CRR² 26.

eg.p: See comsad.

egForm.p:
= cobsaid: Ri comḟossaid, SR 16. macaemh
ceillidhe comhḟossaidh, FM v 1822.18. Appar. n. pr.in:
orgain Cathrach Comḟossaid, Met. Dinds. iii 242.15. Cf. corad comfossad comnart, SR 5078.

(fostaid): go n-imat sliūs chomhfhostus ┐
imtheilges in t-uisce restrains, Fl. Earls 40.4. Part. an
tionglan cruaidh comhfhosduighthe = coacta, 23 K 42, 205.18.

(fossugud) act of maintaining, holding out: tucc-
sat . . . cúl ré comhfhosucchadh a ccathlaithreach, FM v
1628.8. gur luaithigheadar . . . cos(aibh) ré cómhfhosúghadh
ré tarann ain (tarrachtain, v.l.) áigh `to hold firm', CRR² 40.

(fot). Also com(ḟ)at, comot, cubat. equal length
(of time or space): comfat eim na sceine
a knife-handle's
length, Laws i 132.20 Comm. da chomfot na h-amsire i
parrthus isin amsir acainde, LB 230 marg. inf. secht milí
ní comod suaill (cheville), BB 300a26. con derna so in
comfhad so . . . i slait mair (of the Cross), YBL 136b35. is
e comfad do dhíon a dheagh-chotun D., .i. . . . go a glun
the extent to which, MR xiii 25. lan iarraid fon comut re
`in proportion to the length of time', Laws iii 310.20 Comm. re
comat rudartha `during the period of prescription', i 80.32
Comm. comfad cuirp in cath-miled na thomhas, MR 260.4.
co fuair lícc a chomfat `a stone of the right length' (for grave),
Dinds. 91. Hence in concrete sense grave: comfot C. ┐
a arad, Dinds. i § 28 (RC xv 283). comfot, Dinds. i § 28 = cubat, LL 3860. coro lásat c. doib
tóeb fri tóeb, Airne F. 153. cubat fom thaeb, cloch fom
chinn, Fél. 90.1. Note also: naoi lēige a chomfhat, lēige
amhāin i n-a leithet
length, Fl. Earls 86.14. As quasi-adj.: ní
comhfhad bhíos barr na mér
are not of equal length, Studies
1924, 243 § 15. ? slis comfat tocht troimfer, Dinds. 42.

In adv. phr. in c. sin (cétna) for so long, equally long: a
fuirech in comfot cétna
for an equal length of time, LU 3128.
in comat sin `a corresponding period', Coibnes 9 gl. 14.
do mhair an comhfhad céadna, TSh. 91.

As conj. in c. while; as long as; as far as: i (leg. in ?) com-
fhat ro bátar immi sain snigis tromshnechta, MU² 306. in
comfhat bís . . . i n-a chuilén, PH 7415. in comfat beth i
(sic leg.) cuibrech, Laws i 106.23 Comm. Note also: an
comhfhat aimsire ro buī ag briathradh fri Petor, Fl. Earls
208.20. in comad ro sia a barr `as far as its top would ex-
tend' (of a tree), Laws iii 226.11 Comm. mana ro mo guth
in comfot congrur, v 190.3 Comm. See comméit, 2 cubat.

(2 fót): i comfod ┐ i comfhaire watching together, MU²
220 v.l. (comóit, L. comfoit, Y).

(fota) equally long; very long: o tuind Clidna comḟada,
IT iii 89.19. cona n-dib cael-crannoip comfata, CCath.
4717. is c. ar cech leth (of a lake), Dinds. 158. Prov. ni
comḟada ḟásas gach slat, Ériu v 142.4. ni comḟada barr
na meur, 8 (see comḟot). As subst. (equal) length: clarland
. . . credhumha i comḟata ┐ i coimlet[h]an in creasa sin,
CCath. 5230. comfota dótbuindi dedhlaeich, Grail 884.

(frecarthach) corresponding: na cúig nuim-
reacha . . . dlegar a mbeit comfreacurthach do na cúig
féiltib, O'Gr. Cat. 312.33. an comhartha . . . comh-
fhreagrach don mhí in a mbia, Corp. Astron. 106.7. As
subst. do gabar a comfrecurthach in cach bescna dib in
ḟocail is eitget, O'C. 897 (H. 3. 18, 399).

(frecra) act of answering; answer, correspondence:
cóir do chách a coimhḟreagra, Met. Gl. D.1. in da fid
aireghda i comfrecru, Auraic. 5460. coimfrecra nan foladh
nard, Laws ii 314.22 Comm. teagasg . . . a modh comh-
fhreagartha
question and answer(?), Flower Cat. 588 § 2.
ag coimhfhreccra a chéle (of animals), Hugh Roe² 146.6.
re comfregra in catha `to attend the battle', MR 194.8.

(frestal) act of attending to, waiting on: cuairt
fregra C. do chomḟresdal `respond', MR 162.1. duni no
chongbad sciath comrestail imbualta do `who could hold a
shield . . . with him', Cog. 166.12. setig a chomrestail
a
suitable wife for him, LU 10164 = coimfrestoil, ZCP iii
231.3 (cf. dingbáil, D 127.85 ).

(frithgnam) joint service, attendance: fellsom ┐
fer cóm[ḟ]richnama . . . do A., Alex. 542 = coimfrichnuma,
ZCP xxx 123.1. umun comhfrichgnum `as regards co-
service', Laws v 296.9 Comm.

eg.p:
(fritháilem): ro gabh for comfrithailemh in
dá stiurasmann `began attending', CCath. 2023.

egForm.p:
(frithorcun): an dufurgaib in chomfrithorcun
ón gl. conlisio (coll-), Ml. 138b1.

eg.p:
(fromtha): luirech comhḟromtha `a proof coat
of mail', ALC ii 292.10.

egForm.p:
(fópairt) act of (mutually) attacking: uair roga-
bhadh aga ccaitheamh ┐ agá comhḟuabirt `proceeded to
shoot, strike . . . them', FM vi 1986.13. 2032.23. v 1824.18.

(fóbartach): isin caithfes comhfhúabartaigh
aggressive, Hugh Roe² 314.20.

(fúachad) act of (violently) stirring up, mutually
assailing; strife, opposition: conad he cet adbar comuachaid
(comfuachda, v.l.) Thana bo Cuailgne, Ériu ii 176.20. in
uair bhus cóir in comhfhuachadh, Cath MT 218. cēd-adhbar
a gcomf[h]uachaid, ML² 6. fer fúair tighernus . . . gan
comhfhúachad, Hugh Roe² 278.14. tre coccadh ┐ comh-
ḟuachadh, FM iii 48.3. a cluinsin ag comf[h]uachad re
fiallach na foraire, ML² 358.

(fúachtae): re caismeartaibh cómhfhúachda na
g-curadh very fierce, ML 128.24.

= comḟúachad: tria frithbheart ┐ comh-
ḟuachtain a chloinne budhéin fria roile `contention', FM v
1610.13.

(úaigid) unites, joins (fig.): ro comhfuaigh . . .
gluine geinealaigh . . . A., BNnÉ 251.35. comfuaigeas
. . . Eoin in aisneissea `combines', Fen. 4.1.

(úaigthe): clárdroichet comfuaighti `tied together',
CCath. 1403. 2385. cliaibh-ionar cómhfhuaidhte `well-
sewn', CRR² 27.

(úarad): an corp . . . ar gcomhfhuaradh grown
cold, TSh. 1090.

(fúaslucad) mutual release (of prisoners): T.
. . . do lecon amach ar comfuaslacad ┐ G. `was released in
exchange for G.', Ann. Conn. 1340.5 (without ┐, FM iii 568.11,
AU ii 464.8). a leiccin amach a comfuaslacad, 1389.7.
comfuaslacad bragat, 1393.8. fuair siomh a mac . . . do
comhḟuasgladh as na braighdhibh rémraite
had his son re-
leased in exchange for, FM iii 244.13.

(fúasmad) mutual smiting: do comfuasmadh ┐
do comtuaircnigh a n-arm, CCath. 3170. ro thogbhodar
comḟuasma[dh] cogaid fria Galloib `an insurrection of war',
ALC ii 426.15.

(comḟúasmad): cogadh comhfúasmadach
etir Brían . . . ┐ Laighnibh `a mutually aggressive war', ALC
i 2.15.

(fúatach): bó cacha cind comfuataigh
a cow for
every joint plunder(?), Anecd. ii 75.7.

i, m. (fuil, see Thurn. Gramm. 171). Later also
comḟuilige. commuilidi, BB 241a45 (cf. comḟolbthaige,
comm-) blood-relative: honaib comfulidib echtrannaib .i.
ar comfulidib ar chuit ceneuil gl. consanguineís, Ml. 66d1.
dia chomfulidib fessin `to his own kinsmen', 67c2. na
tabraid coicill . . . do carait no do comḟuilidhi (= -ige),
CCath. 5162. comat derga airm chaich assa chomfhuiligi,
YBL 173b27. roadnaic cach . . . a chomfialusa ┐ a chomuilidhe
`relatives', Ériu viii 56.6. a chairde ┐ a chomhḟuilidhe,
FM v 1772. 15.

(ā, f.] (comḟuilid): dilis do P. ó c. ┐ ó iris =
consanguinitate . . . fide, Trip.² 718 = o comsuilidecht (.i.
o comthoil), Arch. iii 18.4.

(fuilngid): comfuilngid na háo ris suffers jointly,
Rosa Ang. 274.20.

c. coarfichbem coemchlanna C., Corp. Gen.
79.13.

eg.p:
(fuirmiud): is comḟuirmud forgnúsa tantum ┐
ni comsuidigud `a collocation of a form', Sg. 203a2.

(fulang): tri comfulung [na mball ele] `through
`sympathy' with the other members', Rosa Ang. 138.13.

egForm.p:
(fuláirem): ar comhfurailemh righ ┐ righ-
thaoisech joint command, BNnÉ 207.2.

(comḟortacht) med. helps, comforts, relieves:
neithi comfurtacht[aighes] iad, Rosa Ang. 44.23. ni com-
furtachtaigter an naduir on leiges, RC xlix 24 § 6. com-
furtachtaidh an cumne, O'Gr. Cat. 275.20.

(by-form of prec., cf. Engl. comfort) helps, con-
soles: do chomhfhurtaigh an t-aingiol é (of Christ), Parrth.
Anma 5379. 5655. do chomhfhurtuigh tú mé, Is. xii 1.
comhfurtaigh ré hubhalluibh mé = stipate me malis, Cant.
ii 5. Vn. fear a gcomhfhurtuighthe = qui consoletur eos,
TSh. 4390.

(comḟurtaigid): do bhéura sé comhfhur-
tuigthéoir eile dháoibh = Comforter, John xiv 16. xv 26.

eg.p: see coimge.

(gabáil): comhghabhail ar ttráth
the singing of our
psalms together, Eriu v 94.31.

egForm.p:
(gáel) relationship, kinship: ara chomhgaol, BNnÉ
281.8. aos cumtha is comhghaoil
friends and relatives,
KMMisc. 242.27. Concr. relative: ro marbh a caraid ┐ a
comgael, St. Ercuil 2272. gan a beth do comgæl agum
nech ecin etc. `kinsman', ZCP vi 94.17. ar tresi a braithrech
┐ a comghail, BCC 158.27. Cf. comhghaolta `kindred',
Eg. Gl. 156 (adj. ?).

(cf. gabtha): dona gáib cómgaibthib `festgefügten',
Alex. 261.

(gáibthech): trí sróna . . . cómhgháibhtheacha
`importunate', ML 120.5.

(cf. coimge ?): cin cach óin dia comget / tét
foraib co bráth `every one whom they protect', O'Dav. 696.
ar ḟuil, ar ḟcóil romchomga (romcomda, MSS.) `for the flesh
that protected me', Ériu vi 115.1.

(cumang): do comhgaing spirat a mathar = quasi
sine spe anxiebatur, Smaointe B. Chr. 1141.

eg.p: see congáir(-).

egForm.p:
(gairdes): ní fuil . . . acht cómumla ┐ cómgáirdis
united joy (of heaven), De Contemptu 1251.

(1 gaire) proximity, nearness. In prep. phr. i c.
near: a c. doib, RC ix 16 § 5. foran ccaladh ina chomh-
gaire, BNnÉ i 235 § 156. a c. re hinbleogain, O'C. 1759
(23 Q 6, 35 a).

(comgar): ro chomhghairset dhoibh drew near
to
them, Hugh Roe² 180. 18.

(gáirid): cómhgháireann sé leis an nduine bh-
fírinneach
rejoices with, De Imit. 297.23. do chomgháireadar
coin . . . ┐ badbha
cried out together, CF² 1062.

eg.p:
(gairit): an ccom[airet] (comhgairid, v.l.) boi ac
ibe
while he was drinking, TBC 6186.

egForm.p:
(gáiriugud): comgairiugud a mbidbad . . . impo
`the shouting', CCath. 2781. comhgáiriucchadh, FM v 1614.14.

(gairm): `feib' feabhus cách dha chomhghairm
called by all, Met. Gl. D. 31. comhghairm náomhtha con-
vocation, Exod. xii 16.

= con-gair: clann in pāpa comgairmither dīp
they are called, Fl. Earls 176.18. Cf. congairmim, ZCP v
503.15 = congairim, IT i 141.11.

(cf. comgar): cing Artúr . . . cáirdeamail comh-
gairseach `neighbourly', Ó Bruad. iii 68.12.

(gaisced) equal valour, experience in arms: a
cheile comhghaisgidh ┐ comḟoghlama, ZCP x 276.10. aes
comhghaisgidh, Hugh Roe² 90.2 `allies in the fight', Gloss.
With gen. or DO: fer a chomgascid `a warrior of the same
training', Táin 1885. comalta comgaiscid do Th., TTebe
3826. cach fer comchliss ┐ comgascid do I., LL 30968
(TTr.).

eg.p:
(comgaisced): comalta c. `comrade in arms',
TTebe 4662.

egForm.p:
(gait) joint theft: urradh cána comithi ┐ comgaiti
`participation by . . . joining in a theft', O'Gr. Cat. 100.17
(O'C. 2568) = O'D. 654 (H. 3. 17, 484-5). arna haisnéis a
c. sellaigh, O'D. 1175 (H 2.15, 44(68)b).

eg.p: see congalar.

ecis aidbsin .i. fili c. bhís la righ, O'C. 473 (H. 3. 18,
248). Cf. canaid?

form.p: (gar)

egForm.p:
I [o, ā] (equally) near, ready: corup c. comdiles
don tuaith, O'C. 1990 (H 4.22, 25). ba c. bas dó, Grail
4307. comhghar é dá n-ionsoighedh
equally near (of death),
Dán Dé xiv 2. Superl. an lóchrann lasas go mear / is dó as
chomhghoire caitheamh, Content. xxiii 10 n.

form.p: II As subst. o

eg.p:
(a) proximity, nearness; shortness: ragatsa
. . . an comngar dia nindsaighe
the short cut, D iv 2, 58rb15.
sé an bóthar mór is mó comhgar (prov.)
the shortest, SG ii
554.44. go gcomhghar mara ┐ tīre i n-a himfhoixe, Fl.
Earls 70.20. dul i gcomhgar cheithre rian `a place where
four roads met', Keat. ii 2685. a gcomhgar trialloid im-
thecht `in a short space', Duan. Finn i 72.z. ar mbuain ó
chomhghar a chéile `kept apart', O'Hara 2877. In prep.
phrases
near (to) with gen. or DO: ata cathair . . . ar comghar
duindi, ZCP vi 72.24. ar c. Ercuil, St. Ercuil 2192. riccit
. . . ar comhghar a chēile, Fl. Earls 10.32. i gcomhghar
dhuibh, DDána 102.29. táinic . . . G. . . . a comghar co C.,
CF² 196. dul i gcomh-ghar rachas mé / d'onóir bhar n-aicme
uaisle `the close criticism I shall proceed to make', Content.
v 12. Note also: mana fuil cintach a comhgar re hinbleo-
gain, O'C. 1759 (23 Q 6, 35 a). fo chomhghair (leg. -ar?) na
cceathra `in the direction of the herds', Hugh Roe² 146.9.

(b) convenience, expedient: do chum a chómghair féin do
dhénamh de `to use as may suit him', ML 184.2. ó nach fuil
comhghar dhar gcóir (`neighbours to do us right'), Ériu i
16.15. teirce sóidh, aoibhnis, ┐ chomhghair chorpardha,
Desid. p. 14 n. gusin uile ch. ┐ riachtanas, Fl. Earls 66.y.

egForm.p:
(comgar) near, convenient: atá sibhse dho bhí . . .
neamhchomhgarach, ar na bhur ndéunamh comhgharach
=
made nigh, Eph. ii 13. i mboith chumhaing chluthair
chomhgraigh. Hackett xxvi 92. Superl. is comhgaraighi ┐
is imfhoixe, Fl. Earls 100.7. Adv. más féidir é go comh-
garach =
conveniently, Donl. 236.11.

(garg) (equally, very) fierce: na catha cródai cómgharga,
Alex. 127. da chert-bheim . . . chomgarga, MR
298.20.

(comgairm). As subst. M. a chomhgarmach
crier, FM i 138.z.

eg.p: see com(ḟ)ocus.

egForm.p:
(gataige): ma tainic comgataide leis accomplice
in theft, O'C. 1651 (23 Q 6, 21 a). da comgataighe, ib.

(gainithir): caraid . . . dumha do-comgin for
medhon a méise .i. . . . imad in neich comgeines, isin mbiu
[.i.] in t-inathar `of what is produced', O'Dav. 751.

(gel) (equally, very) bright, fair: na fir coimhgheala .c.
ó bheith geal uile dhóibh, Bard. Synt. Tr. 41.17. ar mo
shliastaibh coimgela, TFrag. 10.16. 'na c[h]orp c[h]omgeal
`all-white', BColm. 30.1. ceinn-berti comgela, MR 266.26.

(gell): do gheallus . . . fám chomgheall . . . go mbeinn
. . . pledge, BNnÉ 222.13. As n. pr. Coel ┐ C., LL 353b50.
See coingell.

vn. of con-gella. act of mutually promising, con-
spiring; conspiracy: fo c. M. `under a promise of help from
M.,' RC xviii 9.2 (Tig.). de conspiratione Iudeorum .i.
. . . an coimhgelladh ┐ in mi-run do-ronsat na hIdhail i
n-ághaidh Crist, Smaointe B. Chr. 2784. fiss droch-ruin ┐
coimgeallta, 2935.

(geóin): comge[o]in na sochaidhi `clamour', CCath.
3133.

(gerán): ic comgeran ┐ ic comaicaini `wailing
together', CCath. 1082.

(gíallnae): no (for no a n-, or in-, Ed.) déiti i
comgialla `the (? their) acknowledgement in equal hostageship',
Ériu xvi 183 § 39. is la rig cach . . . bis oca oen comgiallna
dó, O'C. 1998 (H 4.22, 28). cairdiu no comgiall[a] la
flaith for flaith naile, 471 (H. 3. 18, 247).

eg.p:
i lleinid (leg. -ib ?) leth-gealaib literda lan-c.
gacha caingni `in the plain context of the written narrative',
MR 270.7.

arnabtis c. (of cattle), O'Mulc. 298. Perh. part.
of con-boing.

egForm.p:
(glaine): c. . . . fri etrochta rétland equal brightness,
LU 2095 (FA).

(glanaid): ro chomglan crechta a cnis `she
cleansed', TTebe 2101.

(1 glas) joint fetter: an fer do baí ina ch.
his fellow-
prisoner, FM iv 840.15.

(2 glas) very (equally) grey, green, blue etc.: forsna
cloidmib comglasa, LB 152b32. súli comglassa cíchurdai,
LL 32337 (TTr.). co roscaibh comglasa caínnleacha, BB
427b1.

eg.p: see coingleic.

egForm.p:
(gléire) extreme brightness: connaibe fo chomglére,
SR 720.

(gle(i)th) act of grazing together: amal nacethra
ic[c]omgleith (: leith), SR 7224. ag . . . c. do fri blichtu,
ZCP xiv 351 § 9 `which grazes with milch cows', Laws ii
244.24.

(glenn): innaslebe ┐ inna comglinne gl. convalles,
Ml. 81c16 (`coined', Edd.). i comhglendaibh sleibhi H.
`glens', CCath. 5632.

(gleo): a g-cóimh-ghliadh `single combat', Oss. iv
108.13.

(glinne) joint security: do aisneis a c., Laws i
294.1 Comm. ní bí coblach na bí comglinde, O'D. 2217
(Nero A vii, 149a). See next.

(perh. to be referred to prec.): cingith carpat
comglinni, TBC² 1818 (rhet.) = comglinni, LU 6334. Cf.
is com glinni dothéig ar mo chendsa, 6690 = co ṅglinni,
TBC² 2148.

(glóraigid): ón Mhac, . . . chomhghlóraighthear
ar aon leis an nAthair = conglorificatur, Desid. 4934.

(glúair): S. . . . / crechlasrach cathglicc comgluair
very brilliant, LL 15867.

eg.p: see con-glúaisi.

egForm.p:
(glúasacht): do neoch ro chumhaingset do
chomhghlúasacht
all they could drive along (of cattle), Hugh
Roe² 80.w. dár ccomhghlúasacht do chum grádha =
to
move vs to, RSClára 38b. do chomhghluasacht mhór gaoithe
┐ sneachta `commotion', Corp. Astron. 30.33.

= comglúasacht: dar gcomhghluasadh dochum
cuimhnighthe orra
inciting us, Luc. Fid. 3280.

(gnás) earlier -gnas (see Fél. cited below) company,
companionship, association: is maith for comgnas (con-
sonating with ingnas), Fél. Ep. 379. iar comgnáis ┐ comat-
trib na colla, LU 2077 (FA). RC xxvi 148 § 28. mo chur a
comgnais aṅgel. SR 1763. bai coicer inna comgnais (: tlāis),
7640. ni fuibean Abraham ar comgnais fri Ner ┐ Erccol,
O'D. 971 (H. 3. 17, 679c). comhghnas .i. comhghnaoi uais
no uasal, O'Cl.

eg.p:
(gné?): c. cuíniud Conaire, BDD² 1055 (congne,
v.l.) = comgné caíniud C., LU 7452. `having the same form',
Plummer MS notes.

egForm.p:
O. oirdnidi / . . . / caindel comgnidi (-ghnithi,
v.l.), IT iii 55 § 104 `made, fabricated', Meyer Contribb. Cf.
gnethi s.v. gníid?

(gním) congnim, IT ii2 191.2 (cf. congnam) joint
action, co-operation; (equal) prowess: ní dene ch. frisin
pectach du chuingid comsóinmige fris gl. ne emuleris, Ml.
56c15. is leu dorignius chomgnimu gl. innocentibus coniungi,
47a20. roindfid C. c. fri cach n-óenfer, LU 7103 (BDD 77).
7153 (83). t'ḟer . . . comgascid ┐ comgníma `the man who is
your equal in . . . prowess and great deeds', Táin 2728. triar
churad comgnima, Acall. 7122. in dá ech . . . comchóri
comgníma
equally active, LU 9255. cen rimad comgnimha
fri forcetal co-operation, BNnÉ 305 § 22. As vn. ro gab ic
coimhgnimh inn imairicc `began to join in the fray', CCath.
3644. Legal: isedh is comgnim and, mac ac imain ┐ cuaille
ac teascadh. Is edh is cen comgnimh ann cechtar de dib do
foghlugudh i necmais a ceile
collaboration, O'C. 2340 (Eg.
88, 26(27)a). cin fir comgnima
liability of an accomplice,
Laws iii 116.24 Comm. trian n-aithgina a n-aes comgnima,
v 156.19 Comm.

(gnímrad) joint actions, co-operation: a fhear
comgaiscid ┐ comghnimartha
equal prowess, RC xiv 260.8.
in naes comgnimraid `fellow-labourers', Laws iii 168.1 Comm.
mad ro fetatar is lucht comgnimruidh iad uman ngait
accomplices, O'D. 442 (H. 3. 17, 340).

(gnúis): tíre . . . / ata comgnúsi cadli `whose aspects
are lovely', Imr. Brain 11.

(gail): an chomhghoil choccaidh contest, Hugh Roe²
188.30.

eg.p: see conguin.

egForm.p:
(gonta. cf. gonaid): i gcliabh chomhghonta an
choguais contrite, TSh. 441.
(2 gor): Críst in c. (: om) pious, LL 38340 (SG 371.2).

(gothach): comhghothach, fuaimneach = ec-
choing, Eg. Gl. 286.

form.p: (1 grád)

eg.p:
(a) equal rank or standing: iarná ccomh-
gradh choir, Ériu xiii 34.8. cách ina ccomhgradhoibh lá
tuaith, 33.6. folog cech gráid ecalsa fó ch. túaithe, Críth
Gabl. 488. a comgráda do thabairt for neoch
to confer
equal ranks with themselves, Ériu i 218 § 3. ba ceim comlan
comgraid ndil / i comdail inglanaiṅgil
dignified, SR 4603.
dán bas chomgráid frit grádso
of equal standing with thee,
LL 14598 (ZCP xii 272, xx 193). In cheville: comgrad
ṅgle, SR 4179.

(b) person of equal rank or standing: a ch.
his peer, Críth
Gabl. 28. 114. 205. da comgrad d'inraicaib (of king), Laws i
78.20. o rigaibh cona comgradaib `and their compeers', Coibnes
4 gl. 1. da chomgraid (sic) ┐ di chompersain, Ériu vii 158.30.
a réir neich bun chomgrād dó, i 219 § 7. See congraid.

egForm.p:
(2 grád): ar tabairt comgrádha dóibh araen do
equal love, CF² 26.

(grádach). Adv. go connail comhgradhach
very lovingly, Ériu v 88.10.

(1 gráin): fo chichurdacht ┐ ch. horror, LL 31969
(TTr. 1155).

(gráinemail): na briathra cómhghráineamhla
`hateful', ML 122.17.

(gressaid) urges, incites: comgres cach, TTebe
2286. 3056.

(grian): a duibhfine na gaibad c. comfogais equal
land, O'C. 2234 (Eg. 88, 17(18)a).
(grind): c. cóir very exact (chev.), SR 4505.

(1 grith + 1 gráin): ri c. in churad, LL 32538
`at the horror of the hero's shout', TTr. 1739.

(grotaid): ag comghrodadh in catha ┐ ag feithem
a bflaithrígh expediting, Caithr. Thoirdh. 108.30.

(gúaillid): a comguaillidhi (-idh, v.l.) imruma
féin fellow-oarsman, CCath. 1991.

(guide) act of praying together; joint prayer: ic com-
guidi dæ frinni, Ml. 53b15. in comattach-sa ┐ in chóm-
guide forru, LB 225a13.

(cf. guinid): congnamaigh echraide . . . Aliter
c. .i. aiten `equally wounding', Auraic. 5580.

(comgus, see com(ḟ)ocus): céim le caoinbháidh
comhguiseach `the love of his kith and kin', Ó Bruad. iii 88.6.

eg.p:
(gol): comhghul do dhéanamh ris
to weep with him,
TSh. 6009.

egForm.p:
(guth): i gcómhghuth le ceol-sheinm in unison with,
Keat. Poems 111.

(íadaid): rochomiadsad . . . imi
they closed
around
him, TTebe 3279.

(íarraid): comiarraigh na minn joint seeking,
O'C. 602 (H. 3. 18, 294c).

(íartaige etc.) (common) descendants: Iacob araen
re claind ┐ re comiartraige, BB 239a37. a cinedh ┐ a coimh-
iarttraighe, BNnÉ 234 § 152.

gs. (comícc): brog a c. `the farm of his neighbour',
Laws iv 124.10 .i. a comaithig, 18 Comm. fri tir in c.,
120.15.

(ícc) act of paying; (joint) payment. As vn.: is fiach
indligid do coimic doib eturru(d), Laws ii 56.15 Comm.
duais do coimhioc, Ériu xiii 16.24. Concr. fir ┐ gell, comic
┐ comlaine (the four things that perfect law), Laws i 260.x.
comic iar tairmtecht `payment', y. comeas cána ┐ cóim-íca
`the tribute and the payment', BR 184.4. lucht cóimícca
Ch. C. `tributaries', Hy Maine 62.1.

(1 íccaid): comicad etarru `they . . . pay equally',
Laws iii 120.21 Comm.

(dp.) (idu): fo ches is fo ch. `in anguish and labour-
pangs', Met. Dinds. iv 130.84.

(idbart): creidim ┐ c. do denam (joint) sacrifice,
Laud 610, 8c cited Plummer MS. notes.

(imdae): 'ma cethrib c. very numerous, TTebe
3148. ? commaith bfairgsi ┐ fesa / coimimdha modh maith-
esa, IGT Decl. ex. 163.

eg.p:
(imm-foilngi): madh ann com[i]mḟuilngi
eissidh
causes jointly, O'C. 1615 (23 Q 6, 6 a).

egForm.p:
(imḟolang): slan dona feraib bis a[c] comim-
fulang a feirgi `sustaining', Laws iii 236.z Comm. Cf. a[c]
deg com imulang a mbochta `supporting', 20.5 Comm.

(imlán): don chraoibh chomh-iomláin cnuas-truim
`perfect', Content. xxix 18.

(imm-lúadi): long . . . for a comimluaiter na
ráma
in which the oars are plied together, O'Dav. 478. maina

coir ro comimluaitet na cuir, Laws ii 306. 10-11 Comm.

43.

(imlúad) (joint) motion: ni coimimluadh cuirp
comfhoicsighes nech do Dia, Lism. L. 712. mada frecru
in giall in fechium toicheda co comimluadh gell do taircsin

(imbed): c. na gaíse superabundance, LL 24309.

(immáin): ag denam cluiche ┐ coimhiomána
`playing and hurling together', BNnÉ 244.3. tigsom com-
ludh no comimain friu-som, RC v 199 § 8.

eg.p:
(immaircide): c. gl. conpetens, Ml. 131d2.
comimmaircidi gl. hora conpetenti, BCr. 39c7. ordugud
comimaircide na n-epert or[di]natio congrua(m), Auraic.
592. With adv. suff.: in chomimmaircid[id] gl. conse-
quenter, Ml. 55c22.

(immaircidetu): honchomimmaircidetaid
gl. consequentia, Ml. 36d5. inc. gl. consequentia, 37a11.

(cf. imna, imnaid?): comimnaidhe cathge .i.
a clainde, O'C. 1988 (H 4.22, 28).

egForm.p:
(imrád): go roibh comumradh (sic) ceille codh-
naigh aigi deliberation, O'C. 1770 (23 Q 6, 37 a). nocha raibe
comimradh denma na fogla `intention', Laws iii 156.16
Comm.

(imm-rádi): comimraiter a n-dernsat a n-dís
`what both achieved is reported of one', MR 250.8.

(imram): for combáig comimrama rowing match,
LL 32154 (TTr. 1343).

eg.p:
cach comimridh .i. foimrim iar ndechmaid, O'C.
513 (H. 3. 18, 259).
see coimitecht.

egForm.p:
b[ī]aid dano ōigi c. in commond crāibdiuch,
ZCP ix 450.26 = cominad ōigi
centre of virginity?

(inunn): cominund dealg `a similar brooch', Laws
ii 148.1 Comm. na trí Pearsona . . . coimhionann = equal,
Donl. 24.17.

eg.p:
(indell): tuc a chois 'na ch. `in his own engine',
Met. Dinds. iv 122.z. ? acuiriu comindel comthoicthe,
Corp. Gen. 80.27. mintire; cominnull tuaithe, Laws ii
12.24 (`central territory'). fer difaesaim, .i. comgraidh no
ap no munap min tíri no c. tuaithe `regulation of the territory',
i 90.28 Comm. is eicin móirṡeiser ag gabail athgabala
. . . .i. mintire, ┐ [cominnell tuaithe], 226.2 Comm.

egForm.p:
(indligthech): masa comindligtech iat `equally
inadmissible to give legal evidence', Laws ii 350.16 Comm.

(indocbáil): diambemni hicombás bemmi ic.
gl. ex mortuis `in common glory', Wb. 24a10.

(indraic) of equal worth, equally reliable, etc.:
coir coirpdire c. `honest', Laws iii 536.11. fiadnaisi choitcend
c., O'C. 1744 (23 Q 6, 31). O'D. 1580 (H 5.15, 7a). triar
coitcenn c., O'C. 2080 (H 4.22, 68). .l. cumal comhinnraic,
LL 392d29. as radh coitcheann coimhiondraic do ghlain-
lebhraibh . . . E., Ms. Mat. 572.30.

(indsma) act of socketing, riveting together: ar na
com-indsma a curpaib a ceile `were mutually socketted in
each other's bodies' (of spears), MR 254.20. In metrics of
special kind of dúnad (see Murphy Metrics p. 44, Henry,
ZCP xxix 94): c. .i. índsma in iarcomairc isin tsillaib
tuisig nama ut est do .i. donnchad, IT iii 80.4. c. do Dond-
chad Do, Auraic. 2199. c. is coir dia ndunad, 2214.

(ingaire) joint herding, grazing: co ber breith im
coningairi (sic)? O'D. 1569 (H 5.15, 4b). comur ┐ comingairi
ris in mbráthair, ibid. comíngaire . . . : cia cruthsaide a hur-
lainn garachceathra ┐ sealb? Laws iv 100.4 Comm. cominghaire
eturru fein, v 322.19 Comm. comar ┐ c., ii 56.23 Comm.
v 330.10 Comm. ni dó rainic in la sin in comar no in c.,
O'C. 1716 (23 Q 6, 17 b). ? cuairt cominghairi, O'C. 515 (H. 3. 18,
260).

(ingelt): i cuairt comingelta co-grazing, O'D. 1571
(H 5.15, 5a). See coingelt.

eg.p:
(inmain): amail budh cominmhain leis uile iad
as if he loved them all equally, BCC 436.10.

egForm.p:
comairb .i. c. .i. [leg. ut est] fer elgnais o cin
cin comoirb a cein, O'Dav. 463 joint repelling (?), cf. indarba.

(in-árban): uair nar cominnarbustar uadha i
céin in fer laimhe derge
did not banish, O'D. 767 (H. 3. 17,
550) = comindarbustar, O'C. 1256 (H. 3. 18, 507).

(indisin): clú ┐ comaurdurcus ┐ c. in sceóilsin,
LL 30965 `account', TTr. 146.

(indraice): teid . . . fo cominnrice frisa foasc
it is equally valid
with . . . , Laws iv 106.9 Comm. (Ériu ix
33.1).

(indsaigid) joint or mutual approach,
attack: masa comindsaig (sic) do tarb echtrann, Laws iii
232.19 Comm. coimhionnsaicchidh doibh fair `they made a
joint incursion', FM iv 1168.15. ? cominnsaighe re feche-
muin ar bidbuidh, O'D. 767 (H. 3. 17, 556-1). mas tall
dlegar a tabairt is cominnsaigi, ┐ mas amuigh is comiarraigh
na minn, O'C. 602 (H. 3. 18, 294c).

eg.p:
(indas): is inann condealg ┐ comortus nó c. nó
comaontu, O'Dav. 517.

egForm.p:
(insce): dorónsat . . . comluga ┐ c. `confederacy and
alliance', TTr.² 560.

(minugud): clogaid . . . ag c. `broken to pieces',
Fianaig. 90.11.

(airgal): c. Congail ┐ Conain `joint battle', MR 250.7.
cech coimhiorgal ┐ cech comlann, TBC p. 593 n. 9.

eg.p:
baile . . . i-mbi c. sida itir na fechemnaib
`ein friedliches Übereinkommen(?)', Cóic Con. Fug. 57 § 133.
Perh. = com-arrachtu, Ed. (82 § 74).

(airsaire): arisdochruth comirsire nadesse `unseemly
is the barking(?) of two', Wb. 13a6.

egForm.p:
m. (Lat. comes) gs. in c., CCath. 60. np. -te. count,
comes: commiti ┐ cennturi, CCath. 5775. a coimite ┐ a
ndictodoire, Trip. xxviii 14. las in c. dianad ainm A.,
Todd Nenn. 70.7. Fig. is tossach cacha tedma ┐ is cet-c.
gacha moruilc (of famine), CCath. 2354 v.l.

eg.p:
(itg(a)id: co rocomhitchem ind ūan
that we may
earnestly beseech, Otia ii 100.4.

egForm.p:
vbl. of necess. of con-éitet (Thurn. Gramm. 444).
ní boc. dó `he should not be indulged', Wb. 1c12. nad come-
testa dó, Mon. Tall. 151.12.

(ithe) act of eating with, banqueting, devouring:
comithi gl. commensationes, Wb. 20b21. hoc c. ann, IT iii
237.73. ic coimhithi in feoir `devouring', CCath. 3506.
maille fri coimhithe chuirp a chompáin, Fl. Earls 234.22.
? urradh cána c. ┐ comgaite, O'D. 654 (H. 3. 17, 484c) =
O'Gr. Cat. 100.17.

(cf. Lat. jus, juris? Plummer MS. notes): is c. (com-
diuir, condiur, v.ll.) in Coimmdiu `equally just', Fél. Prol.
229. .i. is comdíriuch hic hícc na maithe ┐ hic traethad na
n-olc, Fél.² xxv. O'Dav. 1100. comiair .i. comdirach,
Stowe Gl. 297. ? coic cressa caini c. (: dúir), Rawl. 77b20 =
comthúir, LL 16161.

form.p: (-ae) d. f. (cf. con-luí). IGT Decl. § 7.

eg.p:
Valve of door, window, etc.; lid; covering: c. .i. com-lūt[h]
.i. coma lūas tūas ┐ tīs, Corm. Y 236. haec valua c., Ir. Gl.
125. comhla .i. comlá thís ┐ túas, Ériu xiii 67 § 75. comhla =
a gate, portcullis, grate, Eg. Gl. 140. tech miodhchuarta . . .
dronchaol a ch., Ériu xiii 40.16. im comhlaidh a thighe,
14.22 = imcomlainn, O'Dav. 376. cosmail comlaid ōir / ūë
Luirc Labraid, Ält. Ir. Dicht. 41 § 30. di brisiud a chomlad
(-ai, v.l.), Críth Gabl. 214. cup c. `hopper' (of mill), Laws i
124.19 (see Mann. and Cust. i ccclx). derc hi cinn na cobla
`at the end of the door', Cáin Ad. 2. c. for cach senisteir,
SR 188. di senistir déc and co comlathaib glainidib fríu,
LU 8733 (FB 55). tech . . . eter fraig ┐ lár ┐ chomlada,
Fing. R. 418. córaigis comlaid cen chol / forin tiprait `lid',
Met. Dinds. iv 66.y. noco ndech c. fri haieór (of an im-
possible eventuality), ZCP viii 111.15. c. umaide, LB
152b2. comhladha gloinidhe, Ériu iii 156.20. do sithlaighthi
iatt tresin comloith n-io[i]rn amail ciaro tré línanairte, Aisl.
Tund. 97.7. mé ar cúlaibh a comhladh (of heaven), DDána
37.30. cor eich ní chaigle go comhlaidh `thou dost . . . drive
. . . Thy steed up to Hell's gates', Aithd. D. 77.27. a raibhe ó
slabhradh na comhladh asteach (of castle), FM v 1638.14.
caithfe an dorus dá chomhlaidh do bheith air =
two sides,
RSClára 27b.

egForm.p:
Extended applications: rogab iarum att in ingen . . . ┐
rodún a comlaid conustacht a hanail `her door' (
uvula ?),
Dinds. 21 = comlaich, LL 27722. comhla dearc súlchorr
Sadhbha eye-lid, DDána 99. 32. ar comlaid na slige
the door
giving on to the road. Y Cymmr. xiv 104.11. mo cumachta
a comlaid mo chlaidim, TTebe 1309 v.l. (comlai[n]d, text).
a ch. sciath na Héirenn (to a shield). Arch. ii 146.26. Duan.
Finn i 34.11. Fig. comhla an bháidh `the door of love',
Aithd. D. 71.10. lé comhlaidh chean, TSh. 1651. eochair
an cheóil ó sa ch. (of a harp), Mann. and Cust. iii 258 n.
Freq. protection, shelter: Petur . . . / . . . / mo ch. nach camm.
KMMisc. 256.14. c. cōicthi thūaiscirt hĒrenn, TBC² 3338.
do sgiath réidh, comhla na gcríoch, Magauran 2071. a
chuilinn . . . / a c[h]omhla re gáoith
shelter against, Buile
S. 66.6. comhla re fearuibh fiach, O'R. Poems 683. Note
also: comhla re rún ríogh Teamhra / síol Eadhra ar cúl na
comhla, O'Hara 3961-2 (see n.). Of warriors: c. ergaile,
LU 4842 (TBC). ina c[h]omlaidh chothai[g]the curad (of
warrior) `protecting door-valve', Fianaig. 86.9. in c. catha,
Cog. 188.6. Cf. a c. catha . . . .i. a scieth, CCath. 4721.
in Chomla Chatha Cheltchair, LL 12514 (Ériu iv 28). As
n. pr.: trí meic Ersand ┐ Chomlod, BDD 1345.

(labairt): ag cómhlabhairt ris an fear úd con-
versing with. Eochairsg. 101.15.

(labra) joint speech, dialogue: act of conversing:
asné gnim tengad c. gl. omne quod loquimur, Ml. 31b24.
in ch. gl. allocutio, 46a15. airbert biuth c. `the use of speech',
59a10. comlabrai in choimded `the words of the Lord',
31d10. tua co comlabra, ZCP iii 447.4. combo réil a com-
labra, Thes. ii 338.44 (Hy. v). fuaslaicter go comlabra fir
`an utterance of truth,' Laws v 496.3. c. . . . ┐ imagallim,
┐ aisneis (requisites of witness), O'C. 2180 (Eg. 88, 6(7)b) =
comlabrad, 1183 (H. 3. 18, 469b). cen chomraid, cen chom-
labrai, SR 4374. a n-dligheand . . . rí C. is comhlabhra
is a matter for discussion, BR 218.29. adhbhar ceoil ar
gcomh-labhra, Content. xxv 1. As vn.: ac comlabra con-
versing, Táin 1605.

gl. primae . . . personae possessiuum `allocutive',
Sg. 204b1.

eg.p:
(lobur? lubair ?): as c. doib uile, Laws v 466.21
.i. na cethra is comfand, 470.16 Comm. ma comlabair no
ma comuaisle, O'D. 540 (H. 3. 17, 433).
iar comramaib crodaib comlabur, BB 432a31.

egForm.p:
(comla): don chúirt chomhlaigh, DDána 119.22
`strong-gated', Ir. Monthly 1923, 642.

eg.p: see cumlachtaid.

egForm.p:
ni tuillidh in direta feich comladha dó, O'D.
712 (H. 3. 17, 520).

(laíded): sgiath . . . aga cómhlaoidheadh ina
cheart aghaidh being brandished(?), ML 84.19.

eg.p: see coiblige.

egForm.p:
(lagat): a thobhach iar [g]-cóimhéad ┐ iar [g]-cómh-
laighead in cach bliadhain `be it great or be it little' (of a
tribute), BR 184.6.

(comlann) evenly matched (of armies): uair
robtar comlaindech, YBL 197b36 (BB 259b22) = ar ba
coimlín doibh. RC vi 174.12.

(comlán) completion, fullness; perfection: c. cride
┐ menman, LL 37542. conuaige .i. cocómlaine, Fél.² xcvii
5. comic ┐ comlaine `fulfilment', Laws i 260.24. iar com-
láni
completely, LL 31471 (TTr. 656). iarna comlani
un-
impaired, Auraic. 153. comhláine = integrity, RSClára
131a.
