the breast of the man, Acall. 1812. dar compur a chléibh, LL
8437 (TBC). hi fforfholamh a chleibh ┐ a c[h]ompair, FM v
1716.5. tri choimpir a chraóis `through the body of his gullet',
RC xxix 142.10. sgoltadh compair a chroidhe `the bursting
of His breast', Aithd. D. 78.24. tre ch. . . . a cuirp, MR 286.3.
i compraib a chele, Celt. Rev. vii 214.28 (compur, TTebe
402). ic reidiugad reme-siun / chompair cacha cath-laithrech
`obstructions', MR 184.15.

eg.p:
Compd. síol na gConn gcomparchairthe, DDána 89.24
`a bhfuil a n-uchta mar chlocha(?)', Gloss. (see Eg. 1782 49a1
cited above).

form.p:
(Lat. comparatio). Thurn. Gramm. 226, 569. In
later lang. comp(a)ráit.

egForm.p:
(a) Gramm. comparative degree:
ní derscaigi in c. di hilib a cheneiuil fessin gl. comparationem,
Sg. 40a6 .8. c. gl. comparatiuum, 41a6. di c. gl. in com-
paratiuis, 43a6. sech positi na conparite (leg. com-) oa
mbiat gl. comparatiua, 45a8. isin comparait, 39a29.
comparaiti gl. comparationes, 26. ainm comparaiti `the name
of comparative', Auraic. 693.

(b) comparison; act of comparing: comparáid gl. collacio,
comparatio, Ir. Gl. 896, 875. gan comparāid incomparable,
Mac Aingil 160. 'na ccompráitt
in comparison with them,
Ms. Mat. 567.16. cum a ndéntur na coimplex ele do
compraid = ad quam complexiones aliæ comparentur, ZCP
xviii 262.36. ni heslainti hi an tan sin aca compraid cum a
crichi = vient à bonne fin (of therapeutic intoxication),
O'Gr. Cat. 216.33. a ccomparāid ris
comparable to him,
Desid. 5773. a comprāit sin d'onōir, Fl. Earls 188.27.
compráid = respectus, Celtica viii 203. mar chompráid, nó
mar stoc maguig
figure of fun, Párl. na mB. 306.

eg.p:
(comparit): in c. (recte chomparitith, edd.) gl.
comparatiue, Sg. 44a4.

egForm.p:
m. (Engl. loanword) compass, circumference, circle;
extent: ar cuma leth-compáis
in a semi-circle, Maund. 69.
do reir spere no compais comcruind, ZCP vi 59.3. ar a'
ttaobh astig do ch. t'umhlaoidheachta (chúmpáis, v.l.)
within the scope of, Párl. na mB. 947. faoi ch. radhairc
gach duine
within sight, Corp. Astron. 164.11. messait . . . a
fhod . . . fri compāss in tige `in comparison with', Fl. Earls
128.17. Of the navigational instrument: puínntidhe an
chompáis, Párl. na mB. 190. snáthad an chompáis, Mac
Aingil 792. Of mason's instrument: hoc equicium .i. c. no
raing antshair, Ir. Gl. 1137 (see raing). hoc equilibrium .i.
compas, 1138. Note also: an c. nár chúrsáil tar chiomhsaibh
(of a wise leader), Ó Bruad. ii 178 viii.

(compás): deich gcolamain chasta chompāssacha
circular, Fl. Earls 216.18.

eg.p:
(pennaid): c. fris `does the like penance', Ériu vii
146.z.

egForm.p:
(persa) person of equal rank: di chompersain,
Ériu vii 158.29. itir da compersain, O'Don. 1641 (H.
5.15, 19a).

eg.p:
= compersa: compersainna, Laws i 212.27
Comm. compersanna ca (leg. cach, Plummer MS notes)
celi eclasdacda co eclasdacta, O'Don. 1576 (H. 5. 15, 6c) =
1641 (19a) = O'C. 528 (H. 3.18, 264a).

form.p: ā, f. vn. of con-beir.

eg.p:
(a) Appar. some kind of legal
judgment or decision, but precise meaning unclear: comperta mbroga`criteria of land', Ériu xxii 83.5 c. .i.
combreith [ut est] itir diablad creich [creth F.] comperta,
O'Dav. 351. fear na coimperta aca rad nad indath cinaid,
O'C. 1389 (H. 3. 18, 630b) `the man who pleads', O'Don. Suppl.
cia leth coimpert inarbtha brethe no airbert ae, O'C. 2271
(Eg. 88 f. 20 (21)b) = cia leth coimperta indarbthar
breithemnas etc., 1608 (23 Q 6, 5 a). c. .i. fairsing, ut est:
tuca dochridhe c., Ériu xiii 77 § 217. cain bearar fiachu
cairdi i coimpeartaib catha glossed comairbeartnughadh,
O'C. 1906 (23 P 3, 21 c) = caoin beradh fiach cairdi coimperta
catha na tobaing egen na forbflathus, na anfis, 2257 (Eg.
88, 19(20a). fearr ni cearchaill comraici comaide, co feisir
coimperta comlaithre co nach tairce difolta dait, 1889
(23 P 3, 22 b). fir . . . comperta naime `the test . . . of the
holy draught', Laws v 470.35 = combruithe noebe .i. is o
Dia in combruith hisin .i. cairi fír; vel sic in aliis libris,
compertae noebu, etc., 456 note 1 = fir combruithe noebe,
H. 3.18, 391b10 (Plummer MS notes compares the `water of
bitterness', Num. v 11-31). do coimpertuibh-breat[h]
Fíthil ann so, Ériu xiii 30.21. coimperta Fiothla breth
bunadh fíor fasach, 22.

egForm.p:
(b) conception, act of begetting, procreation (cf. Lat.
conceptio, conceptus): combart do sarre `that Sara would
conceive', Wb. 2c23. adbar inna combartae cloine gl.
conceptús, Ml. 71c6. toglúaset chombairt `they abort offspring',
Thes. ii 235.5. do glan coimpirt agealuain, Blathm. 97.
ilar comperta `sexual unions', BCrólige 57. cis lir lanamna
. . . comperta do-cuisin la Feniu ? `Paare . . . der Zeugung
(von Kindern)', Stud. in E. Ir. Law 16 § 4. airiadad
coimperta, BCrólige 38. C. Iohain . . ., Fél. Sept. 24.
combart cen peccad, IT i 133.4. cethir do ch. (sic) dam,
LU 4248. acht go léightear a gcoimpeart `if you read the
story of their conceptions', Content. v 84. a bhféil a coim-
peirte, Parrth. Anma 3579. Attrib. gs. amser chomperta,
LU 1656. inbaid comperta, LL 14406. uair choimperta,
MR 172.9. As genre of stories (in saga-list): na cuimperto
.i. Coimpert Conchobair, etc. birth-tales, Anecd. ii 44.12.

eg.p:
(c) In more concr. application offspring, produce,
child(ren): aurail coimperta i soaici `Zeugung (Kindern)',
Stud. in E. Ir. Law 26 § 7. ni berat comperta for fine `they
put not their progeny upon the tribe', Laws v 272.12. ite
andso comperta mbroga fo a luibid `such then, are the
productions of land', iv 278.31 Comm. a chlain[n]e is a
chomperta, BColm. 12.26. na ren in coimpert (viz. the
infant Brigit), Lism. L. 1185. ? daig ní fhulṅgitis c. Duind
Cualnge accu, TBC 1532 `begetting', Táin p. 174. coimpeirt
geoid
goose's egg, MR 110.5. guth na circe / ag commaoi-
dhamh a coimpeirte, Éigse i 118.13.

egForm.p:
(d) semen virile: hoc sperma. coimpert, Ir. Gl. 847. in
ch. . . . rolásaide . . . it maclocsu, LL 35686. rothoit a
coimpert uadh, Fél. 134.37. ambra sperma ceti .i. coimpert
an mhil mhóir, 23 K 42, 349.3 .

(compert) act of impregnating: ar comperta
corptha .i. coimpertnug[adh] a cuirp fri daine umdha,
O'C. 2239 (Eg. 88, 17(18)c).

(prísúnach) fellow-prisoner: má (sic) chomh-
phriósúnach, Phil. 23.

f., Trompa na bhF. (modification of comlucht?)
company, gang: a ch. brúidhte brónach, E. O'Rahilly xxii
185. Lucifer 's a chúmplacht = Lucifer et ses compagnons,
Trompa na bhF. 839. an chomplucht uile = toute la
compagnie, 4945-6.

(pócad): ben is fer icompocath kissing
each other,
TE Eg. 10 (IT i 125).

(Lat. loanword) computus: ? an c. m erdha, Ériu
xiii 37.8 (O'Dav. 285). do réir an údair compoidi `according
to the compotist (named Lincolniensis)', O'Gr. Cat. 289.26.
an féarsa compoidi so `this compotus verse', 302.36.

(compoid. See Ling. Val. 72) art of computus:
sói ṡenchusa . . . ┐ compóidechta, ALC i 524.10 = ┐
compoitiachta, Ann. Conn. 1301.4.

(compoid) computist: dá teagmadh dermad
. . . ar compoidigi, O'Gr. Cat. 307.18.

(Lat. loanword) camphor: ola ┐ finegra . . . ┐ c.,
YBL 345a29.

(Engl. loanword) comfort, consolation, joy: a bheith
mar ch. agam . . . iodhbairt . . . do dhéanamh
that I may
console myself, Párl. na mB. 990. Freq. in Trompa na
bhF. (see Gloss.): gan súil le c. = soulagement, Trompa na bhF. 1461. an
uile shórt compóird = toute sorte de joye, 45.

(compórd): gach nídh dá chompórdaighe
every
kind of pleasure, Trompa na bhF. 643.

(Engl. loanword) composition (
Perrott's) (see
Ling. Val. 128): na ro chuir a lámh ar an c. sin dorónsatt
`ordinance', FM v 1842.13. maille lé composeision, vi
1996.6.

eg.p:
(compráit s. comparit): comprāidigthear risin
craidi = comparatur, RSláinte 90.
see comrar.

egForm.p:
o (on gender see Thurn. Gramm. 448. Cf. comrag
mbairdne, O'C. 2773 from Eg. 88, 82b). Vn. of con-ricc.
comrag m., IGT Decl. § 11 (54.18), Verbs § 65. With final
-g in class. verse, in other late texts often with -c (cf. D 297.
81-3). (act of) meeting: encounter; freq. in military contexts
battle, fight: a chomraicsom frisaul `of his encounter with S.',
Ml. 75a1, a chomraicsom ┐ Saul, 6a. c. (cobrac, MS.),
Thes. ii 237.10. iar comruc ind crontsale frisind laim `after
the spittle touches the hand', Mon. Tall. § 38. c. a thoíb ri
talmain, Met. Dinds. iv 38.40. comrug gen curu bel
`combat', Laws iv 32.4 (of single combat for the purpose of
enforcing a claim). derged comraig nad fornastar, v 476.24
cf. c. .i. tobhach, O'Dav. 364. airligud seoit fris' tabair
nemed c. i n-airliccud `opposition', Laws v 372.2. in
comruc comarleicti `pitched battle', 148.13 Comm. in c.
tulla `sudden collision', iii 254.18 Comm. do chomroc fri
fer, LU 5081 (TBC). tri .xx. crand / comraic (leg. comrac ?)
nad chomraic a mbarr
whose tops all but touch, 3703 (SC 33).
fo-cheird in colcc ndét sin a n-airde co tuit for cenn ind
fir . . ., c. nat comraic fris
without actually touching him,
TBC St. 4458. A. . . . ba cruaid comhroig (: goid), BB 59a47.
dorala in cath ina comracaib `the battle fell into duels',
TTebe 2828. do chomrag . . . ┐ do chomhdhluthugadh a
g-cairdeasa `to unite', MR 96.10. comhrag dá bhall ríogh
sa rathoigh meeting (of Christ and the Father), Aithd. D.
70.21. With qualifier: cen ch. n-oenḟir
single combat, TBC
1232. c. fir re fer, ML² 1870. re coimríac[h]tain dúin c.
n-immairic `before we met in conflict', Táin 3418. a comruc
deisi
in single combat, Aen. 2288. Attrib. gs. re comraic
`a battle', Laws v 300.26. a chath-eirred . . . comraic, CRR
34. re dliged comraic, O'C. 1772 (23 Q 6, 37 b). a chéile
comhruig, IGT Decl. ex. 590. ag fuireach ret fhear
gcomhruig (: dhuid) adversary, Aithd. D. 8.37. For cáer
chomraic see C 19.74 ff. With vbs. see do-beir, do-gní,
feraid, fris-gair, fúacair.

eg.p:
Of sexual relations: ba coindme a c. (of Cú Chulainn
and Findabair), LU 6060 (TBC). iar c. dó . . . frisin mnaí,
LL 35728. is hē mac ruccad and din chomruc sin, ZCP
viii 309.13. c. ar eiccin re mnaei H. `to rape', CCath. 3845.

Of seas, territories, roads, etc.: comruc na n-ilmuire
where many seas meet, Corm. Y 323 (of Coire Brecain) = c.
na n-ilmuiri aniar ┐ anair, Dinds. 145. i comracc da ferund
border, BB 253b8. a comrag Allban ┐ Saxan, Ann. Inisf.
1307.1. do ch. in dá ríg-lind `meeting of the two royal streams',
Met. Dinds. iii 32.78. for comruc teora sliged, LL 36387
(RC viii 154 § 4). comhrac `a corner, a meeting of two ways',
Eg. Gl. 200.

Other applications: a c. an chathbha[i]rr ┐ na caemh-
lúirighi, CF² 185. a ccomhrac a chinn ┐ a ramhar an
mhuiníl `base of the head', Ériu viii 139.26. hi cc. chorráin
a gheill ┐ uachtair a bhraghat, FM vi 2114.y. a comrug
da rand bis in gach aisde acht an debhidhe sgailte ┐ a comrag
da leathrand bhis inti sen (of fault called ráen)
between two
quatrains . . . two couplets, IGT Met. Faults 72. a comhrac
an lae ┐ na hoidhche
at twilight, Atlantis iv 168.23 .
see comarc.

egForm.p:
(commar): folt clandbuíde c. wavy(?), BB 427a35.
Críoch M. . . . / in mhōrchomrach (: ōrchornach)
of great
confluences, Butler Poems 693. ? Celtchair c., LL 14270,
leg. comracach or comramach(?), Plummer MS. notes.

eg.p: see cuimrech.

gan techt slán úadh ní hingnadh / imdadh úar clár
na comhradh, IGT Decl. ex. 541. ? Cf. 1 cobrad.

egForm.p:
(rád) ? cobrad, Arch. Hib. ii 48 § 6. gs. -áid. Note
also as. comraid (: comdail), SR 4374. Pl. comrada, TTebe
718, SR 8310, in later lang. comrái(d)te. comrádh comráth
m., IGT Decl. § 11 (54.12). Verbs § 83.

eg.p:
Act of conversing, talking; dialogue; speech, utterance,
saying: comrad clocán bind, LU 9845. guidem frisin-
morchomdid / in cech húair ar comráda
to speak to us(?),
SR 8310. c. chind cherchailli pillow-talk, Táin 3. 278 (title).
ba c. cach dessi ┐ cach thrír díb
they chatted in groups of two
and three, CRR 13. cach coirmthigi a chomrād, Arch. iii
226.22. ? cor ar comrād fri Canōin `intentness on(?) con-
versing with the Canon', Ériu ii 65 § 11. gáini (leg. gainne)
a comráid, MU² 717. gan c[h]omrād Dē
converse with God,
Arch. iii 234.14 `not praising God', Aithd. D. 61.6. i comrād
`talking together', BColm. 90.25. tre comradh L.
because of
L.'s words, St. Ercuil 885. é ré cách ag comráth (: thráth),
IGT Decl. ex. 396. Verbs ex. 822. cuirim i gcomhrádh
I
mention (specifically ?), DDána 32.13. an tí choimhéadfas
mo chomhrádh-sa = sermonem meum, TSh. 2854. Transf.:
fóir mé le comhrádh do chuirp, Dánta Gr. 30.43. Phr.
cóir comráid (see cóir 8): ō rāinic ar chóir chomrāidh
opportunity of speech, Anecd. i 25 § 7. ro gab coir comraid
frisin ngilla `fit converse', CCath. 4060. toigeacht a gcōir
chomhrāidh re aroile (of ships) `within speaking distance',
Fl. Earls 12.1. Cf. tré cheart gcomhráidh, Ir. Syll. Poetry
40 § 6.

egForm.p:
Pl. is ingnadh lium do comraite
sayings, Fier. 160. ina
rúinib ┐ ina comráitib
confidences, Mer. Uil.² 254. comhraite
umhla millsi. Smaointe B.Chr. 2529. an bladuire léna
chómhráidhtibh fallsa, Párl. na mB. 1518.

corp in curadh comradhaigh, ZCP vi 60.20,
prob. for comramhaigh.

in class. verse -thne (compd. of gni-n-
knows,
O'Rahilly, Sc. G. Stud. i 29. Possibly comráith with
singulative -ne and infl. of 2 aithne). comráithne f., IGT
Decl. § 3 (44.21). `Seems to mean something like equi-
valence', O'Rahilly, but the exx. seem better suited by
fellow feeling, sympathy, kindness, friendliness: ferais ceachtar
de comráichne fri araile
greeted each other in a friendly way,
LU 6065 = comraichne failte fria chele, TBC² 1593 (failte
gloss on text, n.). Cf. comraichne .i. failti . . . ro bu do
buaidh ┐ comraichne sin a Ch. Ch. ol Fergus, O'Dav. 361.
costadh, céol, cumsanadh / connail[be], comraidhne, ZCP
viii 204.9. comraichne ┐ imairchisse[ch]t eturru ond uair
sin, ZCP ii 135 § 11. rostib tond cen tuillem te / nirbo
thuilled comraichne, LL 21987 (Bodl. Dinds. 33, untrans-
lated). ar gcomhráithne re Cathbhaidh
my fellow feeling
with C., DDána 65.18. a chombráithre úaisli is áil /
comráithni úaibsi d'fagháil, IGT Decl. ex. 201. comráithni
trúagh re Torna, ex. 66 with note: `do .b. as cóir
comráithni'.

(comráichne) friendly, kind: in sendam crín
comraithnech (: gaibthech), Acall. 4445. re t'oirecht d'éis
do bráitrech / bí gu cundail comráithnech, IGT Decl. ex. 227.
asum comraichnechsa fria gach n-imnedh `willing to
repair every injury', TFrag. 74.9.

eg.p: see con-ricc.

egForm.p:
(cf. 1 comrac) encounter, battle, contest: ? lainne
a chuaird corcorgemmach / cáera crethir c. / congaib ar
dreich ndendmaisse, LU 7402 (BDD 100). co ruccai calca
crúaidae comraicthi Ulad, 8311 (FB 23). na banaitir
fergnúsi / i ccruadaib comraicthib
in hard battles(?), LU
8427 (FB 29). ? hit ilchomraicib (perh. leg. hi t.), 3495
(SC 26). ger'ba cairdemail . . . in comraicti (comann, v.l.)
sin `meeting', CCath. 2441. girbo chomraicthi dá ṡubach
sámach, Táin 3238. c. flatha, LL 38536. a catha ┐ a
comruigthi
encounters, IT iii 199.14. Perh. a Part. formation from con-ricc.

eg.p: see comrar.

gæ rochomraidh / tria chru icrandghail, IT iii
96 § 150. Cf. con-reith.

egForm.p:
(comrád) converses: ro chomraidsemar fri C.,
LL 31822 (TTr. 1011).

(cf. comroga): do Leith chomhraighnigh Cuinn
(: donnmhailghigh) choice(?), TD 17.32. i gCionn chomh-
raidhneach Coradh, 21.29. See comrognach.

(cf. comrac etc.): sgiath chomhraightheach
chaladh-bhuailteach `fighting', CRR² 74.19 (comhraictheach,
v.l.). comhragach, 80.13. ? bruic . . . chomhruichacha,
Feis TC 32.

eg.p:
ni ch. a ostud, LU 9614 `I cannot help to stay it'
(i.e. a cast), ZCP iii 208 § 8 `I take ch. to stand for chobraim',
n. ? Leg. chumcaim.
see con-ranna.

egForm.p:
(cf. Lat. comparatio `
preparing') intention, design:
c. .i. duthracht [ut est] ni c. do dia n-indichi, O'Dav. 389.
ēol dō inní gonas ūair comrāite ēiside, Corm. Y 548. c. .i.
cuma raidit a cuic cedfada corpardha ┐ a cuic ṡiansa anma,
O'C. 901 (H. 3. 18, 400). ? ar is é ag insin asrenar [comraiti]
na c. la fear asidrean, Laws iii 156.6 glossed: comraiti na c.
athfeghthar and, O'C. 1740 (H 35.5, 80b) = comraiti nad
comraiti, 906 (H. 3. 18, 401) = 2170 (Eg. 88, 5(6)a). comrait
(sic) meic i naes a ica `wilful act', Laws v 434.32 Comm.
fo comraiti ┐ anfot `with respect to intention or inadvertence',
470.1 Comm. tre c. `intentionally', BCrólige 25 gl. 12.
comhraite, anbhfót, torbha, ┐ easbha (list of offences),
Celtica i 101.426.

Attrib. gs.: cinta comraitti ┐ anfoit lanḟiachaig `absichtliche
Vergehen', Cóic Con. Fug. 17 § 5. in coirpdire c., Laws i
176.26 Comm. cin eolgnais c. `intentional injury', v 136.21
Comm. eigem comraiti in codnaig `malicious shouting', iii
244.z Comm. fiacha comraiti, Leb. Gab. 32 n. 8. lethéric
comhraite, Ériu xiii 46.2.

(comrád) chatty, talkative: oireachtus bind
comrāiteach ban, Feis TC 163. re cliathaib . . . cuibdi
comraitecha ciuil, MR 110.21. um an chogur comhrāiteach,
Cath MT `jointly discussing', Gloss. Adv. co ciūin comh-
rāitech, ZCP xiii 170.31.

eg.p:
do conn c. . . . gach nae, O'C. 1770 (23 Q 6, 37 a).
ni caithfe cach acht cia c. asa nemed, O'Don. 2210 (Nero
A vii, 145b). Cf. cotrirther.
see combreith.

egForm.p:
(1 ráth): comaltus ┐ comraith equal suretyship,
O'C. 2464 (Eg. 88, 37 (38)d) = O'D. 571 (H. 3. 17, 442).
in-saigh comhnaidhm comhráith, Ériu xiii 22.9. im
comnaidhm ┐ im comraith, Laws ii 280.6 Comm. comrath
┐ coimfiadnaisi, 282.2 Comm.

form.p:
ā, f. (com + rím; + rám, Misc. Hib. 28. See also
Ped. ii 602). Occas. with ads. -am (LU 3233, LL 12602,
ZCP xi 108 § 1, Arch. Hib. ii 48 § 12). Note also ns. in
chomrama, LL 6224 (ZCP xxiv 140 § 17). Cf. LL 385c16.
? ds. comruma, RC xxiv 184 § 17.

eg.p:
Contest, contention: triumph, victory: comrama et baga
poil gl. bonum certamen certaui, Wb. 30d12. tóxladh crib
comhramha, Ériu xiii 23.9. in gilla sa ata chomrama
óenaidche so ule
successful exploits, LU 9155 (FB 89). dí
ág inna comraime, 3229 (SC 2). ? dia ngabat mo chom-
raimse, LL 6150. do chomramaib Laigen inso (title),
ZCP viii 117. atragat in dias aile / do derscugud chomrome,
LL 4593 (cf. Ériu iv 100.y.). mór do chomramaib gaile ┐
gaiscid, Táin 2197. do chungid chomrame, Sc. M² 16. ? nī
fiu cobraim fri fer marb, Fianaig. 12.z. oīnfer tairismi
comrama frim-sa, Sc. M² 8. racaithed in la re comram
(comrim, v.l.) in cluichi sin `contention', TTebe 2255. staoil
is comhramha clann gCuinn, Content. x 10 (: foghnamha). iar
na ccomhramhaibh `according to their deserts', FM vi 2208.11.

egForm.p:
As vn. oc comraim, Corp. Gen. 31.z. cid do-bérad a mac
do ch. frimsa?
to fight with me, Sc. M² 10. Predic. gs.:
a hoidhed bá chomraime, Acall. 2215. Attrib. for claidbeb
comroma cliath, LL 376a1.

eg.p: See comrím.

egForm.p:
o, ā (comram). comruimech (: fuileach), IGT
Decl. ex. 1168. contentious, victorious; triumphant, trophied.
Of persons: a Chú ch. Cúalṅgi, Táin 1442. ni bat comromach
ar nábat miscnech, LU 3503 (SC 25) = Tec. Corm. 19.25 =
ZCP xv 190 § 37. ic a charait comramaig, Met. Dinds. ii
30.48. recrist comrumach, Fél.² clxxiii 3. As sobriquet:
cath do C. c., Duan. Finn i 89.5. O. . . . comhromhach,
Buile S. 112.20.

eg.p:
Other applications: scíath cnedach comromach, LU 10413.
is glond catha comramaig, 8957 (FB 71). for cirt chomr[a]-
mach Carmain `the contested right', Ériu xvii 42 § 28. re
deilb caem comrumaig, YBL 177b27 (BB 258a16). comsiledh
comramhach . . . mara Ioin `triumphant . . . confluence',
CCath. 265. it cill comhramhaigh
trophied, Lism. L. 4210.
cu ch. `a champion hound', L.Chl. Suibhne 30 (42.y).
Compar. toíseach . . . roba crodha comhramach (leg. -aighe),
Hugh Roe² 286.z.

egForm.p: As subst.: mo chomramaig victorious ones, LL 6154.

(rann, cf. con-ranna). Also cob-. comruinn, IGT
Verbs § 83. Cf. in fíne thic dia cumaroind do reir cirt `to make partition of it', gl. o cirt cobrainne, Laws iv 46.16 Comm. Cf. roinn ┐ comhroinn .c. do rinn (i.e. are per-
missible as a debide-rhyme) ó tá comhruinn ann, Bard.
Synt. Tr. 37.25 (see p. 186). ? as. cobrainne (sic leg.), Laws
ii 176.22.

eg.p:
(a) act of sharing, dividing; share, part, portion: im fabra
mil moir do chobraind, Laws i 124.8 = chomroind. O'D.
499 (H. 3. 17, 402d). o cirt cobrainne `by just partition',
Laws iv 44.8. fis a comrainne (i.e. of stolen property), i
56.15 Comm. do comrainn na bairci (a wreck), 128.14
Comm. 204.24 Comm. ord cobhruinne `order of division',
O'Dav. 1309. eochair cirte comrainn, ZCP vi 270 § 10.
comraind . . . díb
some of them, Táin 3130. adbar comrainne
nad cert, RC xvii 145.8 (Tig.). céin bās aca comroind
while they were cutting it up (of pig), Sc. M² 23. do dálaib
na comrainne
in the division (of quarry after a hunt), LL
1774. mog (= mod) chomroindi co gerr nō co fata
a
classification (of letters), ZCP xii 294.15. ag comhrainn
chreach, Magauran 1086. atá in ruibér . . . ier na chomhroinn
the river is divided (into 12 streams), Fl. Earls 30.13. Of
territory etc.: noco damthadar comraind / do T.D.D.,
Corp. Gen. 119.6. co cobrannaib gall
demarcated by pillar-
stones(?). Corm. Y 683. an ttiúbhraissi comhroinn leithe
Mumhan damhsa? Cog. 214.13. Cf. benn dimor i comhroinn
a dhá su[i]l
juncture, Marco P. 162. Of food: i n-am comh-
ronna `at meal-time', Aithd. D. 75.12. sonus Dé do-roighne
in roinn / gu mbé a Choimdhe ar mo chomhroinn
my portion,
IGT Decl. ex. 1183 (see Éigse vi 73). cūmhgach id
chomhrann, Measgra D. 19.34.

egForm.p:
With prepp. ní dlig comraind curadmír / . . . fri C.C.
to share with, LU 8885 (FB 68). do comhroind críche etir
Laighniu ┐ Hú Néill, RC xxvii 290 § 51. do dherbadh . . .
chomhronda an chiosa sin eter na comharbaibh, BNnÉ
257 § 217. C. sin comrand `in the same stanza' (
in the same
way ? into the bargain ?), Gorm. Sept. 4. ar comhroinn thoir
atá mé `I am lodged with others'. Studies 1919, 74 § 13.
cen chobraind cain (chev.), LL 15659. clanna C. . . . / cen
nach comraind
undivided, 367 marg. inf. Connacht (gen.)
cin comrainn
the whole of C., Ann. Conn. 1315.5. Attrib.
gs.: loighead na codach comhronna fil agad d'Ēirinn
allotted
portion, Ériu viii 135.2. cuit comroindi, YBL 177a19 = BB
257b13. ó mhnáibh comhranna í chealluigh
waitresses,
IGT Decl. ex. 1150. See clad, claide.

eg.p:
(b) partnership, pact, alliance: níptar cuibde comrainne
`agreed in partnership', Met. Dinds. iv 16.8. do c[h]englatar
a comroind ┐ a sīdh, ML² 982. cuid da ḟear dég o Domnall /
ar comraind Cland Conc[h]obair
in return for a pact with,
IGT Metr. Faults§ 80. lucht a comhronna fein `a force
of his own party', AU ii 212.19. a chomhrann cogaidh
ally,
Hugh Roe² 214.23. goma comhrann do S. ┐ do G. `were
mated' (in fight), Leb. Gab. 84.9. crūaid in chomraind
`hard encounter', Arch. Hib. ii 63 § 62. Note also: o rubatur
hisin cobrunn `when they were conversing', ZCP ii 315.24.
? rocelsom ar cobrun (cobra, v.l.), iii 238.5.
See cuibrenn.
see con-ranna.

form.p:
ā, f. Later with ns. comrair and comra with dent.
infl. (see O'Rahilly, Celtica i 351). i gcomhrainn, Ó Bruad.
ii 190.20. comra f., IGT Decl. § 7. comhrair f., § 13 (66.3).

eg.p:
(a) box, etc., chest, casket, shrine: c. gl. capsa, Sg. 36a8.
92a1 (see note). comrara coimge cethre caich torith, ZCP
xi 93 § 27 = c. `Schrein', 81 § 18, cf. comrera, Ériu xvi
65.49. in chomrair co taisib Poil ┐ Petair, Trip.² 296.
co naccai comraid craind, LL 36500. carpat Catháir, c.
(comra v.l.) sét, Met. Dinds. ii 82.29. cómra craind . . . .i.
cómra na crochi coimdeta, LB 159a60. Colmán Comhruire
(-aire, v.l.) `of the Casket', Gorm. Sept. 25 n.5. a cur a
comraigh leis féin (a document), O'Gr. Cat. 265.19. c.
thaisceda sét somainech
shrine for safe keeping, LB 208a54.
See 2 taiscid. badh comhraire coimhēda seanchais É. (of
churches etc.), Celtica i 91.105. Fig. acomhra(i)r derg oir
(of Mary), Blathm. 164. hi comrair gáise
in the safe keeping
of wisdom, ZCP xi 80.19. bása ch. cacha runi, LU 9335.
c. dana, LL 24389 (RC xxvi 52). comhrair bethadh, Ériu
xiii 37.26. comhrair ┐ cisde coimheda eccna
repository of
wisdom (of dead abbot), FM v 1272.16.
See cobrad.

egForm.p:
(b) In contexts relating to death and burial, later
explicitly coffin: ata c. cloche imbi (of buried warrior), LU
10991. rocomecrad . . . comrair don mac . . . don fhid (a
funeral pyre), TTebe 2209. im-medon na c. `coffins', CCath.
894. comrair luadi (ns.), PH 1276. do . . . comraid in
erlama, Laws v 472.2 Comm. ar gcreach . . . do thuill / . . . i
gcomhraidh chumhuing, L. Cl. A. Buidhe 142.108. nochun
ḟuil crann acht do chomhrair
all timber (is bare) save that of
coffins, IGT Decl. ex. 628. fada liom é a ccomhraidh
dhuinn `in a dark coffin', KMMisc. 356.19. comhra, cisde
na marbh, Eg. Gl. 116.

= combras: in chlí c. cond credail
sturdy, Thes. ii
295.3. comrassa vigorous (of horses), LU 10813. co . . . /
cornaib cruachaib comrasaib, LL 35934.

eg.p: see combruth.

egForm.p:
(1 ré) joint (same) time, epoch, reign in phr. i c. fri
(do) contemporary with: . . . bæ i c. fri C., RC xv 280 § 6
(LL 3796). cach duine . . . bói a comhré fris `lived at the
same time', Cóir Anm. 1. í c. nó a comaimsir duibsi, Acall.
4540. With gen.: in ben is ferr delb . . . ina coimre, St.
Ercuil 2427. Absol. E. is C. a g-coimhré, ML 70.20.
Attrib. lucht coimhré . . . dóibh, Acall. 63.

(recht) (joint) equal right, joint or shared law(?):
coir, a comreacht, O'C. 1907 (23 P 3, 21 d) = coir a comrechta,
O'D. 2213 (Nero A vii, 147a) (`just laws', O'D. Suppl.).
? cach bes be comrechta cenn do dib cennuib comrechtuibh,
2201 (Nero A vii, 139b). leó tré choimhreacht . . . / oigh-
reacht, Top. Poems² 453. ? sguir dod choimhreacht re
hÍbh C. `contention', Aithd. D. 31.29.

(réid) (equally) very smooth, level: Cnámrus c., Met.
Dinds. iii 130.38. tri duillendai . . . cómrédi, comalli,
LB 221a45. a críchaib comréidi na Creiti, LL 32000 (TTr.
1186). sinn tir coimredh impao de cech leth, RC xiii 7.12.
an muir . . . amail ba clar cumredh (sic) `a level board', xii
60.10. co tarrla in muir ina clár comréidh, CCath. 1927.
ar chnoc chóimréidh, ML 74.16. Of persons: mairg nach
fuil coimréid má gcenn `agreed', O'Gr. Cat. 369.8. Subst.:
na slighthi ┐ na comréidhi plains, CCath. 2351.

(réimm) equal course, rate; contemporaneity: fogelt
┐ bleth do rith ria a coimhreim ris in athgabhail `at the
same rate', Laws ii 74.5 Comm. a coimreim atait na .iiii.
hernaile sa, O'C. 1041 (H. 3. 18, 435b). alt ┐ dialt ┐ recomarc
i comreim, O'Dav. 428. Ériu xiii 43.27. mac . . . a c. re
nathair
contemporary with, O'D. 756 (H. 3. 17, 545) = O'C.
2473 (Eg. 88, 39b). fo coimrem ┐ comluas `in the same
course', Aen. 995. bás na deise rem dhul féin / meise gá
gcur fa choimhréim `I count as my own death', Magauran
778. gs. as adj.: gur ob croda . . . comremi bar gcuraid,
MR 126.3.

ds. (reimes): T. . . . / i comremis ri S.
contemporary
with S., LL 17738.

eg.p:
(réimniugud) = comréim: ma ta in faesam
i comreimniughadh re dechmaidh, Laws i 100.24 Comm.
ise fath fodera coimreimniug[ad] do lan a ruip a denta
indligthig re lan an duine budhein, O'C. 311 (H. 3. 18, 171)
= i comreimnighudh ris in duine bodein bis cinta a ruib,
993 (425b).

egForm.p:
(remar) very thick; stout: láech cetherlethan c.,
Táin 4400. clóthi . . . comremra, IT i 191.16 (FA 30 LB).
cetha coimhreamra cruinnphiler heavy, Hugh Roe² 332.29.

(répaid): do comhraobadh an gaiste = contritus
est, TSh. 3924.

eg.p:
cengait Lagin ina ndail / fó ch. fo chombáig,
LL 38214 (Bórama). Cf. comrépaid?
see comrar.

egForm.p:
(ríachtain). Also -ríchtain. -rochtain, Leb.
Gab. 128 n. 8. Cf. con-ricc. act of meeting, encountering; meeting, en-
counter: fogur . . . na fial sin oc c., LU 2068 (FA 14).
re coimríac[h]tain dúin comrac n-immairic
to meet in battle,
Táin 3418. ar comriachtuin doib dochum troda, ALC i
570.6. Of sexual intercourse: cinnas . . . nachar chomtig
dun díb línaib comrichtain (Cú Chulainn to Emer), LU
10317. ni fognunn . . . saothar, na coimriachtain, Rosa
Ang. 44.22. gradugud na coimriachtana. Ériu ix 64.28.
gan coimhriachtain ré fear, O'Hussey TC 48.4. Note also:
betit debtha . . . im chomríchtain tossaig nó derid `as to
who shall lead the van . . .', Táin 228. fri comrīachtain friss
to be equal to it (a gastronomic feat), Aisl. MC 75.13.

(comríachtain) come(s) together, has (have)
intercourse: collait ┐ comriachtait na hainmige, PH 7459.
cid b'é fer coimriachtus (-anus, v.l.) ria, De Contemptu
189. do chomhríachtuin sé ría, Gen. xxxviii 2.

(comríachtain): a shíol coimhriachtanuis =
seed of copulation, Lev. xv 16. síol an chomhriachtanuis, 18.

(cf. 2 ríad ?): fo cataid a rig oca mbi i coimriadh
subjection(?), O'C. 2146 (Eg. 88, 3(4)a) (see comríar). ar
forcongair nadurgair ineitet comnirt comriad cond ceill,
2529 (Eg. 88, 44(45)a). ? dosrat fogláed comríada, SR 6794.

(ríagal) joint, common rule: cen chotlud fó
chomríagail, LU 3585 `wedlock', SC2 Gloss. lucht cumta
is coimhriaghla, BNnÉ 283.30.

(ríaglad): ag coimhriaglughadh na seacht
dtuathann jointly ruling, Maguires of F. 98.

(ríar) submission, control, attendance, etc.: tiagat
a comréir cuice, O'D. 560 (H. 3. 17, 439) `subordination',
O'Don. Suppl. fo cataigh rig lais imbi i comriar, O'C. 276
(H. 3. 18, 151). cach comagra for comrér
subject to the same
stipulations(?), O'D. 630 (H. 3. 17, 469). a comriaruibh iar
ndia ┐ duine, 2213 (Nero A vii, 147a). a comdirib, a
comriaraib . . . .i. um a neneclannaib, O'C. 1907 (23 P 3,
23(21d). riched reil / cona chrichaib diacomréir
submitting
to its rule, SR 339. i n-Óe Chúalann fo chomréir `under
like rule', Met. Dinds. iii 116.90. tug siad co[i]mhrēir ar
chealgadh
submission, Celtica iv 109 § 7. i gcoimhréir na
gcliar
attending to the wants of, Magauran 1406. mo cealla
do choimhriar (: riamh) `submitted to my churches', BNnÉ
272.18.

(comríar) attends on, provides for: fir do
choimhriaraigh gach cléir, Top. Poems² 275. más éiccen
duit nī d'íarraid / ar Dhál Cais rot coimhrīaraig, ZCP viii
219.19.

(1 ríata): cidat cuibdi c. inn echradsin well trained(?),
LL 13907.

(richt): vii cumula comrichta
of the same form,
O'C. 2627 (Eg. 88, 53(54)c).

eg.p: see -íachtain.

egForm.p:
(ríge) joint sovereignty; contemporary rule: G. . . . cona
brathair . . . a comrigi .vi. bliadna
reigned conjointly, Todd
Nenn. 68.4. i ccoimhrīghe nÉ. maille le a dhearbhrāithribh,
Celtica i 101.420. C. a comrige fris `in synchronous rule',
MacCarthy 306.1. A. . . . a comrige do T., 308.6.

(rím) act of reckoning (together); synchronising: ní
comrim chloen, Rawl. 88b54. ni cubaidh cen a comrim
not to list them, Auraic. 2023. na rig batar isin domun fria
c. fris, LB 149a20. See comram.

(comrím): cia chomríme, LL 15633 `if thou
computest', Trip. 541.

(rindáith, R 73.37). clóthi . . . comrindaithe
equally sharp-pointed, IT i 191.16 (FA 30 LB).

form.p:
(rith. See con-reith). Earlier comrud (see Thurn.
Gramm. 455).

eg.p:
(a) act of rushing, running together: corba
ch. commadma dina cathaib, LL 32538 (TTr. 1738). di
gréin do ascin i c. in una die
concurrently, 3124. sliabh P. ┐
sliab nO. . . . ic coimrith docom araile, CCath. 4795. saer
he ar a chintaib comaithchesa .i. a beth amail c. a runaway
(cow) (?), Laws v 268.27 Comm. slan do cach fogail . . .
amuil c. nairme stampede(?), iv 156.26 Comm. ag cóimhrith
dochum na hairthighe = recourant (Gloss.), Trompa na
bhF. 4342.

(b) act of racing, contending, competing: ní dene comrud friss
in ulcc gl. noli uinci á malo, Wb. 5d38. do c. fri heacha C.
(of Macha), Dinds. 94 = do chómhruith, Keat. ii 2420.
? comruith (sic) fri nech bis co talmuide `struggling with an
epileptic', Laws i 268.2 .i. comfórithin, 300.9 Comm. (cf.
cobair?). c. fri báeth `competing', Tec. Corm. 14.17.
coimrith fri coin hi[c] cosnum chnáma, Triads 117. ? cach
coimrithe .i. in rith roinne, O'C. 513 (H. 3. 18, 259). ar
echaib cæma comretha
equally swift, TTebe 1513. eich
dubderga comrethi, LL 13897.
see comríachtain.

egForm.p:
(rogu) common choice; equal choice, alternative, rival;
pick, élite: munub comrogha leo maraen
unless they agree,
Laws ii 176.6 Comm. ataat dá thech ma com raghain
(sic)
to be chosen between (i.e. heaven and hell), ZCP xii
395.25. ní fhoil red chlú comhrogha `rival', O'Hara 2966.
ní dá gcur i gcomhraghain
comparing, DDána 37.33. dá
ccuirthí a ccomhroghain a bháis nó . . .
if it was a matter of
death or . . ., Desid. 1613. an comrog[h]a thúas
the preceding
example (two couplets compared), Bard. Synt. Tr. 29.z.
do gleire . . . galgat ┐ do chomraignib curad, MR 224.10.

(comroga) choice, distinguished: saoí coitchenn
comhroghnach, FM iii 486.3. See comraignech.

eg.p: see con-ranna.

egForm.p:
part. of comroinnid (see con-ranna). divided,
severed: do rónadh cethramhna comhroinnte díobh `were
cut in quarters', FM v 1676.w. vi 2258.y. gur bho . . .
comhroinnte . . . a cholann, ML 128.5.

(comrorcun) erroneous, blundering, mistaken:
inna sengrec c. gl. error a quibusdam antiquis Graecorum,
Sg. 6a11. narbamcrimnach comrairgnech
lest I stumble,
miss my way(?), SR 3202. a muinter chorrach cómraircnech,
Aisl. MC 29.21. fiss comraircnech, LB 239a40. As subst.
comroir[c]nich inna nGrec, Sg. 26b6. indegaid nac., 7.

(comrorcun) errs; makes mistake: ocht sillaba
isan focul is mo isan Gædilc . . . anrocomrai[rc]nicsiumarne
`all-the-mistakes-we-have-committed', Auraic. 1436 = inro-
comraircnigsiomairne, 4523.

ā, f. vn. (*com-ar-org-) see conrerortatar. error,
mistake, delusion. In O.Ir. gl. Lat. error. c., Ml. 25d12.
-on, 82d6. -an, 127d5 (Thurn. Gramm. 108). gs. comrorcne,
82d7. ads. -uin, 56b9, Wb. 22a16. -ain, Sg. 90a6, Ml. 14a7.
ap. comroircnea, Wb. 30c21 (palatal group from gs., Ped.
ii 588). comroi[r]cniu, Sg. 1a2 (see Thurn. Gramm. 454).
gp. -on, Wb. 18d7. -an, Ml. 2a6. dp. chomroircnib, 105d4.
Later ns. comrorcu, -co as n-stem (see Ped. ii 111). comrarcu,
Aisl. MC 19.7. ds. comlorgain, BB 239b42 = comrorgain,
YBL 289a1. donrátais icomrarcain (Eve to the Tempter),
SR 1756. ba comrorcu dontí ron ortaig, Trip.² 209. is
cómrurgu dúinne . . . acallaim dé do thabairt do A., Alex.
548 = comrorco, ZCP xxx 123.9. issed fodera in comrorcu
sin dam, Aisl. MC 57.6. tre comrorguin .i. tre sechran,
O'Dav. 1607. in comrargu bunatta `original sin', Aisl.
MC 13.16. comrorco ilair neodair, Auraic. 1716. do'n
comrarcain gentlide, PH 4593. batar i comrorcain fria P.
at variance with, 2510.

(rúad): in ruri garta comruád equally (very) strong,
TFerbe 918.

(rúathar) fierce attack, onslaught: brosgar na
sleagh . . . san ccomhruathar soin, CRR² 35. ina céide
creach ┐ comhruathair `one scene of pillagings and conflicts',
FM v 1688.8. comhluath a gcomhruathar caointe, Hackett²
xxx 77. a chómhrúathar ar na hallmuraicc, CF Eg. 358.
comhruathar . . . ar lucht chathrach M., TSh. 6057.

eg.p: see comrith.
see ruccaigid (R 111.75).
see comrith.
.i. coimét, St. Gl. 302.

egForm.p:
(rún) joint secret, confidence: lucht cogair . . . ┐
cómhrúin, Atlantis iv 206.35.

= comḟosad? co nder[n]satar eturu c. `made peace',
Ann. Inisf. 1114.3.

(sádud): ata mo croidhe ┐ mo smuaintighthe
'arna ccomhsadhadh i noen toil amáin closely knit, BNnÉ
51.25.

eg.p: see coimse.

egForm.p:
(comṡáegul) equally long-lived: gin co budh
comṡaeghlach, Anecd. ii 1.14 = comṡáeglaig, Airne F. 20.
As subst. na comṡæglaig
they of equal span of life, Met.
Dinds. iii 76.134.

(sáegul) equal age, contemporaneousness: comsaegul
Mathusalem immale fri Adam, Rawl. 69b32. bethaduigh . . .
┐ comhsaegal acu re Cael, Acall. 835. Attrib. gs. cloch
comhshæguil (i.e. stone of external soul), ZCP xiii 173.9.

(saer) equally noble, free: tri comurba . . . nis
comsaer a cuir, Laws iii 46.18. mad comsair . . . a cuma
lanamnusa, ii 356.30 .i. commaith a cineal, 358.11 Comm.
ceithri coimperta . . . / uaisli, cuibh[d]i, comṡæra, Arch. ii
140.13. comhdhaor comhshaor, DDána 72.31.

(saethar): mina fuilngi [in gaile] ina comtraothad,
no ina comsaothur `labour(?)', Rosa Ang. 82.9.

(saethrugad, see saethraigidir): do chomh-
shaothrugadh bunadhuis ┐ sēicrēide scēl in tsēpēil `to
investigate', Fl. Earls 126.28.

comhsaighidh .i. comhfhosaighidh no comhnaighidh,
O'Cl. Cf. fossaigid(ir).

eg.p: see con-saig.

egForm.p:
(saíre): equal nobility, freedom: comsaire doib frisna
teora Heoganachta, Cymmr. xiv 116.3. comhṡáeire feraind
C. fri ferand P., Anecd. ii 13.6. comdire .i. comtsaire fria
(.i.) felmacuibh, O'D. 2196 (Nero A vii, 135b). c. ceneuil,
Ériu xvi 180 § 10.

eg.p: see cosmail.

(cf. samail, cosmail): da c. sin do dhaoineib
`men such as they', Maund. 77.
see cumsanad.

egForm.p:
(santach): co comsanntach comduthractach
`longingly', CCath. 2762.

(sárugud): dealb M. . . . do chomhshārugadh `to
commit an outrage on the image', Fl. Earls 62.3.

(sásad): comdídnad (.i. comsasad) great satisfaction,
Trip.² 219.

manap comard na fechamain ni c. a breith fri
dermad tacrad, O'C. 351 (H. 3. 18, 193b).

(scaíled) act of loosing, dissolving, tearing apart:
comhsgaradh no comhsgaoiledh, Ériu xiii 50.5. slan do a
comscailedh (of building), Laws iii 252.22 Comm. in t-ech
. . . do comsca[í]led uadh `to deprive him of', v 438.8 Comm.
ni coimgech comscailedh in feraind
cannot alienate, i 206.28
Comm. gl. roda selba sanna. do niat a comsgailed (a
contract), ii 288.10 Comm. gl. fonuasnat. ag comhscaoiledh
lāmhoigh re aroile `firing at one another', Fl. Earls 188.13.

(scaílid) in Laws Comm. gl. fofúasna, sannaid,
bronnaid: fo fuasnaide a curu uile .i. comscailit . . . , Laws ii
382.10. So also iii 4.17. ni sanntar .i. noco comscailter,
v 444.5. in ferann don tí nar comsgaileastair . . . ni dhe
gl. ma ro bronntar .i. im ní de; no ma ro sanntar, O'C. 2456
(Eg. 88, 37(38)b). ?co ro comsgailed iat tre anfeith, O'Dav.
1255. Note further: comhscaoílter uile ordanāss in baile
`all the ordnance of the place was fired at once', Fl. Earls 40.23.
186.8.

form.p: Vn. comscaíled.

egForm.p:
(scaílte): a cnáma derga c. rent apart, LL 13956
(RC iii 177.32).

do chomhsgair an rígh . . . ┐ do chōimhchrith
trembled, Trompa na bhF. 7602. Cf. do thionnsguin ar
chōimhchrith . . . ┐ do chonsguir (sic) = il commence a
trembler, 5649. Cf. con-scara? comscuir?

(scarad): comhsgaradh no comhsgaoiledh uádh
separation, Ériu xiii 50.5.

(sceinnid): sguchaiss ┐ comhsgeinnis tipra . . .
assin egluis `leaped', Fl. Earls 244.18.

ds. (cf. scís?): cen m'ulchain-se ic c. friat'
ulchain-sea `if my beard wags not in mutual movement with
thine', Aisl. MC 49.9.

(scríbend): eibirt . . . for a n-iada comscribeann
deoda Holy Writ, Laws v 450.3. coimscribinn sein
old
deeds, O'C. 421 (H. 3. 18, 230b).

eg.p: see scríbnid (S 111.35).
see con-oscaigi.

egForm.p:
(scuirid): ro chómscuir a menmain
his spirits were
lightened(?), Alex. 484. Vn. comscur.

eg.p:
(scor): cach do c. d'a gcomlannaib `because all the
others had ceased', MR 268.15.

(sechem): direnaiter crotha cummai c. set `through
following (levying?) of `sets', BCrólige 64.

egForm.p:
(seinm) act of making music, playing together:
a comseinm itir orgán ┐ gitart, ZCP vi 52.8. him chomseinm,
ACC 20 Comm. lan do trumpadhaibh ┐ d'adharcaibh . . . aga
coimseinm, Maund. 255. Cf. con-seinn.

(selb): mad comsealb bes acu araon joint possession,
O'C. 292 (H. 3.18, 160).

(selg): a g-cóimh-ṡeilg
together in the chase, Oss. vi
154.4. Adj. use: na tri Aedana ardda / ropsat cuibdi
comṡelgga, LL 28804.
(seng): Cummin comseng `meagre', Gorm. May 21.

(serb(f)óntaid, -aige) fellow-servant: duine
dhá chomhṡearbhfhoghantuidhibh, Math. xviii 28.

(serc): ro bui comṡeirc re .xx. bliadain eturru mutual
love, Acall. 3392 (comṡercus, v.l.). ar coimsherc ┐ ar cairdius,
Aen. 795.

(comṡerc): cæm incele coimṡearcach very loving,
IT iii 12 § 19.

eg.p: see comṡerc.

egForm.p:
(sessam): na cuirp . . . ina comseasam frisna beoaib
standing together with, CCath. 3172. caithfid . . . coimh-
ṡesamh . . . ó thús go deredh = perseuere, RSClára 77b.

(cf. síans, síansa) also -ṡéns: a comsiansa tuath
.i. a himat cetfaid lochta na tuaithi, O'C. 1965 (H 4.22, 12).
corbo comsens ┐ comcetfaid doib
so that they were in agree-
ment(?), 2023 (49). See comansa.

(síthcháin): fer tiri no comsichána a neighbour
or friend(?), O'C. 293 (H. 3. 18, 161).

(siled): ro ghabh an fuil . . . ic coimṡiledh dar agaidh
S. flowing copiously, CCath. 3670. comsiledh . . . mara I.
┐ mara É. confluence, 265.

(siltech): snechta cruaid . . . c. falling thickly,
LB 118a37. coimsiltec, BB 240a48.

c. iter aidche is lo equal length, LB 102 marg. inf.
Cf. comṡíned.

form.p: (síned)

eg.p:
(a) act of placing (being) side by side: agartha
aicme Míleadh / le chéile 'gá gcoimhshíneadh
if compared,
DDána 85.49. Note also: an toil ag coimhshíneadh ris
harmonizing with it (viz. reason), TSh. 3001.

(b) equal duration, contemporaneity: .vii. m-bliadna déc
dib sin hi c. fri Crist (of Octavius)
contemporary with Christ,
LB 132a27. in tsechtmad . . . / i comsīniud friu huile
of
equal extent with all of them (of ages of the world), ZCP iii
18.22. iar coimhshinedh aimsire gl. iar nedhaibh, Leb.
Gab. 128 n.1. comhaimsir na coimhsineadh neich dibhsidhe
fri aroile contemporaneity, FM i lvi 27.

(c) act of contesting, contending: do choimhshinedh crabuid
fria C. `to contend in devotion', Lism. L. xxii 11. ag iomcos-
nadh ┐ ag coimsinedh re aroile, Leb. Gab. 154 n.2.

egForm.p:
(1 sínte): gach crathad . . . comsinte cuirp very
extended, MR 256.7 (or gs. of comṡíned?). coimhshínte ré
riaghail an réasúin
in accord with, TSh. 3019. 3346.

(síntech): claidmi ailli . . . at e cruaidi comshin-
techa `long-bladed', Aen. 1916.

(slaide): ro gabsat . . . ica comslaidhi severely
smiting them, CCath. 3105 v.l.

(sláinte): asraracht a interiecht ngallraigthi
┐ cosaiti ┐ comslaintiu fri sluagu full health, Anecd. ii 48.15.

eg.p:
ro soich a rob a comsláintinius (sic) ris féin
is equally free of liability(?), O'Don. 1600 (H 5.15, 10b).
Cf. comláintius.

egForm.p:
(slán) quite sound, well, but not always distinct
from comlán: ? comlan adilcae, Thes. ii 236.15 `heil', note
(reading -[ṡ]lán). comslán cach cunnrad amuil do ronad
well secured(?), O'D. 627 (H. 3. 18, 467). gin gur chomshlán
`perfect' (of wounded warrior), Celtica ii 171 § 55. In
follg. best sense given by reading comlán: gu madh ri C. gu
comhshlan `full king of C.', Hy Maine 138.1. niptar comslána
na D (= 500) leo (of a fighting force), CCath. 2686. comslana
cen ní d'esbaid dib, Fél. 230.1 gl. dá chét sescat sláne,
Oct. 30. Compar. cineadh bus comhslaine na bar cíneadhsi,
BB 40a28. Subst. anloisne cach comslán, ZCP xvii 64 § 45.

eg.p: see comlánaigid.

egForm.p:
(slicht?): etir comṡlectaib na cethri sen find fichet
firian, glossed: etir comlechtaib .i. etir comthinóltaib
`groups', Lib. Hymn. 184.12. coimslechta fine .i. comlogh
bidh do damaib isin fine no na cuic tslechta fichet, O'C.
2246 (Eg. 88, 18(19)a). cuimslechta .i. comslointe, D. Mac
Firbisigh cited O'Don. Suppl. Cf. cuimlecht?

(slemun) equally (very) smooth: secht ṅgerrcho-
chaill cíara comshlemna imbi, MU² 626. ola chom[sh]lemuin
cumascda, TTebe 2560. dona cairrgibh coimhshleamhna,
ML 30.26.

(slondaid): cuisle gach cuirp . . . / ón gcorp
comhshlointear (sic leg.) choidhche `is named always from
the body', Ériu xix 102 § 21.

(comṡlonnad): carait ┐ . . . comṡloinntigh
`kinsmen', CCath. 6030.

(slondud) common (sur)name; common stock,
relative: a chomhainm . . . ┐ a chomṡlonnadh `surname',
MR 96.5. cen nach cēille comslonnud
without any claim to
(reputation for) good sense(?), ZCP vi 267 § 9. a cairde ┐ a
cho[m]sloint(h)e relatives, Laws ii 380.14 .i. fialusa, 22
Comm. fine comsloinnte .i. comfialusa, O'D. 549 (H. 3. 17,
437). bá lethan a comṡlonnadh `extensive was his kindred',
TFrag. 62.10.

(slucud): an cathuir do comslucad a fodomain an
talman
would be swallowed up, Grail 248.

(smacht): ro cummaid comsmachtai foraib
they
were given strict orders(?) (of armies), Alex. 184.

(snáth?): cuairt crichid, cobsaid, c. (: ṁblaith),
SR 962.

eg.p: see comnaidm.

egForm.p:
(snaidmid): tait limsa . . . co comsnaidmmer
uar comand ┐ . . . uar caridrad
that I may bind firmly, TTebe
438.

form.p: Vn. comṡnaidm, see comnaidm.

egForm.p:
(snám) act of floating, swimming (in competition):
sechnón in mara for comsnam friu (i.e. with salmon), LU
3089. tonna an chalaidh ar comhshnámh, DDána 113.23.

(snaidid): do chomhṡnoidh cruaidh a chroidhe /
tromghoin an uain ainglidhe broke
the hardness of his heart
(of St. Peter), DDána 20.44.

(sochraid): o Chenannus comhsochraidh (-chrach,
v.l.) very beautiful, BNnÉ 204 § 49.

(sochraite): comṡochraiti na huli Asia, LL
32576 `equal army', TTr. 1778.

(soud) act of changing, converting; conversion: ni
dó rocinn Dia a comhshódh (of Palladius and the Irish),
Lism. L. 232. a comshod co Dia, PH 3346. rath comshóthi,
7917. intí . . . dogní na comṡót[h]i . . . sin, LB 257a37.
comsoid cathimairecc itir da Ua C.
exchange of battle, AU
i 246.5.

eg.p:
(cf. sous): atāt dono dāfodail forfāilte ōniumpaither
inc., Anecd. v 25.2. toruma inraith docum in c., 10.

egForm.p:
(soillse): comsoillse fri etrochta rétland
brightness
like that of the stars, LU 2095 (FA 16). réulta nimhe, ┐ a
ccomhṡoillsi = constellations, Is. xiii 10. Eg. Gl. 375.

(comṡoillse) illuminates, brightens: [ro] com-
soillsig . . . in cuan, CCath. 2751. in locharnn loinnerdai
ro inṡorchaig (.i. ro comsollsig) iarthar mbetha, Arch. iii
8.6 (cf. Trip.² 74). ro inorchaigset (.i. ro comsoillsigset)
a cuicc meoir in mag, 22 § 56 (1447).

form.p: Vn. comṡoillsiugad.

egForm.p:
vn. of comṡoillsigid: do chomsoillsiugadh na
cetharairdi, MR 112.12.

(sóinmige): duchuingid comsóinmige fris `like
prosperity', Ml. 56c15.

(solam): dá chomsolam
two equally nimble ones
(Cú Chulainn and Fer Báeth), LU 6013 (TBC).

(sólás) consolation: gl. consolacio, Ir. Gl. 884. no go
nderna sibh comhsolas linne `console us', BNnÉ 59.13.
in ar companachaib comhsolais = socii . . . solacionum,
BBC 19. an comhshólás thug Críost dona mnáibh,
Eochairsg. 83.23.

(sólásaigid): comhṡōlásughadh spioradalta =
spiritual consolation, RSClára 147b.

eg.p: = comḟolbthaige: c. don athair, YBL 167a9.

egForm.p:
(solus) equally, very bright: combo chomsolus
lá ┐ adaig inti, LU 8056 (FB 2). crích cruth-glan comṡoloss,
Met. Dinds. iv 16.4. indus corub comsolus doib . . . flaithess
Dé ┐ ifren equally visible, BCC 238. ? As subst. c. etir a
failghibh / is a folt
equal brightness, Bruchst. 35 (IT iii
88 § 107).

(solusta) radiant: an ciach-bhrat cómhṡolusda,
ML 102.28. go ccathbarraibh c., Hugh Roe² 152.18.

(somaín): is comsomuin doib
they are equally rich,
O'C. 873 (H. 3. 18, 372b).

(sonus): sí do chur ó chomhṡonus
deprived her of a
great happiness, DDána 58.17.

eg.p: see comḟosad.

egForm.p:
(sreth, `eine gelehrte Bildung', Ped. ii 626).
arrangement, construction, formation. Gramm.: c. gl.
curriculum (ref. to
formation of Lat. wd.), Sg. 47a1.
comṡreithsón cen fodail ceniuil `a construction without
distinction of gender', 152a3. In phr.: tricha coir cubat . . . /
inna hairde i comsreith
in line, arranged(?), SR 2466.
forna cláraib hi comsreith, 4282. See cos(s)ar.

vbl. of necess. of con-sern: bid comsrithi gl.
conserenda est `it will have to be joined', Ml. 16a13; `künstliche
Bildung', Ped. ii 626.

(sroigled): comsroighledh `mutual . . . scourging',
Aen. 2211.

(sruith) equally venerable: ciato chomṡruithi (king
and túath), Críth Gabl. 493. is comsruith a mblicht ┐ a
ngert
equally valuable(?), O'C. 1000 (H. 3. 18, 427a).

(stúamda) equally clever, skilful: comhsduamdha
ód láimh / . . . / gach béas banda, DDána 114.30.

(súairc) equally, very pleasant: ind nathir chóel
comsuairc, SR 1206 (written as correction over chatot).
Cf. a comṡuaircc dalta, Acall. 7454.

part. of comṡúaithid: ac suidigud na mbairgen
comshuaiti cruithnechta `well-kneaded', TTebe 467. in a
criaid chomsuaiti, 4817.

(súaithid): no doirted in n-im . . . ┐ no chom-
ṡuaithed tresin praissig `was . . . mixed with the broth', Fél.
146.26. Vn. comṡúathad.

(súan) deep sleep: cuirris 'na ccomhsúan . . . / B.,
Mann. and Cust. iii 224. cotla na comhshuan do dhéanamh,
Celt. Rev. x 134.12.

vn. of comṡúaithid. act of shaking together, mixing:
cor bo caep-meall . . . ar na comṡuathad, MR 256.13. isin
comshuathadh sin (of wrestling), CF² 704. in chompert . . .
rolasaide . . . tria sin comṡuathad it macloc-su perturbation,
LL 35686.

(cf. súabais?): nidam comṡulbir laburtha (c.
airlebartha, v.l.) frit, Alex. 827 `equally skilled', Meyer
Contribb. 455.

(substaint): bheith a ccomhshubsdaint leis an
Athair consubstantial, Luc. Fid. 4695.

(comṡubstaint) consubstantial: comh-shub-
stantach, ITS xxix 220.27. comhsubsttainteach ris an
nAthair, Desid. 4922. na áoindia chomhsuthain, comh-
ṡubsdaintech, RSClára 144b.

eg.p:
(suí): dá chomsuí gobann
two master smiths, RC
xxiii 324.9.

egForm.p:
(2 suide) act of sitting together, hence parity, equality:
fri dia n-athir inna chomsuidiu gl. consesionis nomine,
Ml. 127d13. comsuide do Dabid frisin comorba, Fél. 54.24
(see Corrigenda p. 470). ni fil asberad istig / bud comsuide
domisig, Anecd. i 14.23 `who could approach me as an equal(?)',
SCano 492 n.

eg.p:
Note also: conid rallá ina chomsudiu, LU 5148 (TBC)
`he collapsed', Stories fr. Táin Gloss. 93.
see comṡuidigud.

egForm.p:
io, iā part. of con-suidigedar. Freq. in Sg.
etc. as adj. and noun (io) compound(ed): bit comṡuidichthi
oaḟograib liter naile, Sg. 4b1. c. són gl. auceps, 8b1. dobriathra
atachomsuidigthi frisnahí siu gl. suscipio, sustuli, 16b4.
21b9. 75a5. 158a2. 201a10. inda rann isinchomsuidigthiu,
202b3. fri taidbech inchomsuidigthi, ibid. inna rainne
dedenchæ in chomsuidigthi, 157b2. Thes. ii 230.22. Sg. 59a6.
175a1. 203a2. 207b9. 211b7. 222b8. focul comsuidig[th]e,
O'Mulc. 860. in comsuidhigthi in focul is eitged? `is the
word e. . . . compound?' Laws iii 94.y Comm.

Med. compound, mixed: 4 áonda ┐ a 4 comsuigighti =
(complexiones) compositae, ZCP xviii 262.30. morbus
compositus .i. galar comtsuigthi, RC xlix 3.7. atá cuid
do na leigheasaibh aenda ┐ cuid ele comsuigithi, O'Gr. Cat.
175.23. ? Cf. oiximeal dúid ┐ commaithe, 23 P 10 ³, 18a7.
commuihi, 17a20.

eg.p:
Note also: comhṡuidhighe (sic) les an Athair =
con-
stituted by, RSClára 144a.

egForm.p:
u, m. vn. of con-suidigedar. comshuided, MR
270.6. act of compounding, mixing, placing (together);
composition. Gramm. oppello .i. ob ┐ pello dodechuid isin
comsuidigud, Ml. 126b10. acobás ṁbís etar ṅdirainn hi
comṡuidiguth, Sg. 2b2. 51a4. 67a18. 139a5. 145b3. 158a3.
159a3. 197a4. 211b6. dlúithe chomsuidigtheo, 203a25.
amuil cach comsuidiugad, Laws iii 94.y Comm. comh-
shuidhiughudh a bunadh `its root is a compound', Auraic.
784.

eg.p:
Med.: tigid . . . annsa comshuigiughadh = veniunt in
commistum, ZCP xviii 262.8. an cumhshuighughadh ceadna
do cur is na cneadhuibh, 23 K 42, 353.18. a coimsuighedh
le baindi, Reg. San. 28.3.

Less precise usages: ? cin cinded cin coimsuidiughadh,
O'D. 1581 (H 5.15, 7a). comshuidhiughadh laetheamhail na
haimsire condition, 23 K 42, 34.8 . suim . . . do bairillighip
púdair ar n-a gcomhshuidhiugadh sa lóchrann
placed, Fl.
Earls 52.27. Cf. [ac]a congnimugad ┐ a consuidiugad
at
its construction (of building), Laws iii 166.z Comm.

egForm.p:
(suilge): cuifre .i. conircli nó comsuilge gentleness,
O'Mulc. 264 = O'C. 92 (H. 3. 18, 66b).

(appar. *comṡon < com + 1 son): i[s] sinechdoig
fil i c. sund, PH 5654 `consonance', Gloss. Cf. saine?

(suthain) (equally) lasting, (co-)eternal: as
chomsuthain . . . dond athair ┐ don spirut náem, LU 2309.
im chumachtu c. everlasting, IT i 169.25 (FA, LB).

dp. (toirt): do comhtartaibh ┐ do misuruibh an
leighis `weights
and measures', Mackinnon Cat. 69.4.

(cf. terbaid?): i nn-oenḟecht c. a ṅgnim, LL
23277 `they used to perform', CRR 57.

eg.p: see 1 comad, commaid.

egForm.p:
(1 tabairt) joint contribution: comtabairt i
cummaid lanamna, Laws ii 356.15 Comm. gl. cumtusa, 5
(Stud. in E. Ir. Law 16).

o (commaid). cumthach c. m., IGT Decl. § 22.
companion, friend: ? dot gleó frit ch. ba gand, Death-tales
20.10 `comrade'. rop c. d'Herind uili / D., LL 19428 (= cenn,
Leabh. Muimhn. 411 § 81). D. . . . / c. comlaind cruad-
chrechaig
devoted to . . . battle, 15915. a cocni ┐ a chara
┐ a ch. P., 31568 (TTr.). nárab cumthach duit ainfhial
do not
make a friend of an ungenerous person, Acall. 602. uair
nír cumthaigh sibh re clainn Caín, BB 22a18. ? bud
cumthach bud comraichne / ra hUltaib inn erṡlébe, LL
6908 (SG 373.4). bá cumthach fríu fó chétóir. LU 1771
`became a comrade of theirs', RC ix 485 (or to be refd. to
cumthach?). a ḟir comthaigh, ZCP xiii 6.14. a chomthuigh
`my darling', A. Ó Dálaigh 1 30. t'fian nach comthaigh
choimhescair
your unwarlike band(?), IGT Decl. ex. 619.
comthuigh áigh, ex. 817. a chomfialusa . . . a chumthach
. . . ┐ a chomalta, Ériu viii 56.7. maille reud chomthachaibh
mairtīreach, Parrth. Anma 4053. Cf. 1 cáemthach.

= coma: do bhraithfinnse comhthaigh maithe
dhuitsi `rewards', RC xxix 132.22. comthacha mora, L.
Chl. Suibhne 30 (42.9). tarcenn ch. mor `great bribes',
Dinds. 133. fa chis ┐ fa comtachaibh `covenants', AU iii 94.13.
Cf. cumhtha `a proffer', Eg. Gl. 190.

eg.p: see cumthach.

egForm.p:
(taidiúir): ag cantain an chíuil cáidh comh-
taidhiúr very sweet, BNnÉ 235 § 155.

eg.p: tóe fri c., Tec. Corm. 12.2 v.l. (comad, text).

egForm.p:
(commaid): do chomthuigh gach teach `visits',
Magauran 252.

(tailc) very strong: rodclái tria gertha c., SR
5470. cathbairr . . . chomthailce, Alex. 14.

(táin) own herd, same herd (oppd. to echtarth.):
a tarb comthana bodein, Laws iii 232.11 Comm.

(táinsem): ? cerd gan comhtháinsiomh, Ériu
xiii 25.7. bar comthánsim for na deeib `your rejection of
the gods', PH 987. o ro-thuic a chomthainsium fen `that he
himself was scorned', 6619.

(cf. comtháinsem) disparages, belittles: ro-
comthánsig a brathriu, PH 1928.

(tairbert): ag comhtairbairt an mhuilinn
`working the mill together', BNnÉ 27.6.

(con-táirci): comtaircidi gl. conlatrices, Ml.
135a5 (see E 158.33 ).

(tairise): claidem . . . cona croseltaibh . . .
comtairisi firm, CCath. 5242.

vn. of con-tairissedar: in fer fil hi comtairisem
frimmsa, LU 9611 = LL 36049 `who is stubborn against me',
ZCP iii 209. ? coitreb .i. comtairisium . . . coitreb caillech
.i. comtairisim caillech n-inglan, O'Dav. 542.

eg.p: see con-tairissedar.

egForm.p:
(toirm): c. na ráma the clashing
of the oars,
CCath. 1954.

(do-srenga): comhthairrngit in chlier rann-
chuid . . . don maiste `drew out', Fl. Earls 52.21. Part.
comthairrngthe.

part. of comthairrngid: an croicenn . . . do
bheith cruaidh comnthairrngthe contracted, 23 K 42, 188.5 .

form.p:
(toísech) fellow-leader: a chomthaisig (np.),
Alex. 489.

egForm.p:
(taisecc) joint, equal restitution: amail ro gabsat
comtaisic im criche (imchríche?) ┐ imaithberta, O'Don. 761
(H. 3. 17, 548). See I 122.28-33 .

(taithmech): do chuibhrighthe do chomh-
thaithmheach
to release you from your bonds, Cath MT 153.

(taitnem) sheen, brilliance: E. co comthaitnim
na clúmi, LL 17043 (RC xlvii 305.23).

(1 tana) very thin, slender: tré chaelcharaidh c.,
CF² 410. an comhthana (a harp), Mann. and Cust. iii 273.y.

(cf. comthanas) accompanies, consorts with: ní
comthana fri échtaid. Tec. Corm. 19.5.

o (commaid, cf. Tec. Corm. Gloss. , Lism. L.
Gloss.) companionship, friendship: fo chórus chóir chomthanais
`in fit order of fellowship', Met. Dinds. iv 60.8.
comann na caradragh na comtanus, RC xi 31.31 (TBC
p. 510). rachindsed a chumthanas
decided to be friends with
him, TTebe 4900. dorala cumthanus mac leighinn in
domuin re B., Lism. L. 1567.

(1 taircsiu): ri c. coma
to offer terms, LL 31629
(TTr. 816).

(tárrachtain) act of meeting, mingling: go
ccomtharrachtain d'iomat dath ann (viz. caer comraic),
Triads p. 39 n. 121.

(tarraing): coin allta dom c. / sair siar
pulling
me in different directions, SG 57.4. Med. contraction: c. na
bhfeitheadh, 23 K 42, 291.10. Of conducting or altering the
course of a river: atā in ruibér . . . ier n-a chomhtharraing ┐
ier na chomhroinn a ndībh rannoip dēg seachnōin na cathrach
`is brought and divided', Fl. Earls 30.13. an ruibēr ar n-a
chomhtharraing i n-a mōirthimchioll `the river surrounds it',
66.30. Of drawing, delineating: armus in diuc . . . ier n-a
chomhtharraing go ro-inntlechtach `skilfully wrought',
252.24.

= tarsna II: na claidhmhi comtarsna trempo,
CCath. 6110. co ndechaid trisin fer c., LL 32296 (TTr.).

(1 táthaid) joins, unites: danaighther contaide
a tadugh cin ainim cin on .i. comtathaig [.i.] a tonn do
comtathugh gan at, gan ainim (of wounds), O'Don. 828
(H. 3. 17, 592). iadhait ┐ comhthāthait le chēile, Fl. Earls
242.29.

(tathaige s. 1 taithigid) frequentation, inter-
course: comhthathaighi etorra . . . ┐ lucht na cathrach,
Fl. Earls 40.12.

(téchtae recte techtae?) equally lawful, valid:
lanamnus comtincuir . . . comtechta a cuma lanamnusa,
Laws ii 356.x. contechta (sic) gnimea no tire `equally valid
are acts or lands', v 332.7. atait dede ardrandat orba fri
mac cedmuintire .i. a c. don tir, O'C. 1995 (H 4.22, 27).

(teclaimid) collection, series: dias is dā fichet
amra / in c. calma (conclusion of a list of kings), Corp. Gen.
128.6.

(tecmáil) act of contending; hostile encounter: oc
imchosnam (.i. a[c] comtegmail) imon rige, Arch. iii 22.25
( Trip.² 1454). ar mhorán do chathaib ┐ do choimhthegmhal-
aibh, ALC ii 446.27. ag comteangmháil. O'Dav. 188.

eg.p: see con-tét.

egForm.p:
(tend) equally strong, firm, etc., but somet. intens.
of tend: cía 'dberar fris cnoc Búi drend, / is é in cotarsna c.
`equal-valid', Met. Dinds. iii 42.38. comrac c.
evenly-matched
fight, Acall. 7080. do da beim comtenna, Cog. 194.16.
